name: 1Day Sooner
description: 1Day Sooner is a nonprofit organization founded in March 2020 by Josh Morrison and Sophie Rose to advocate for people who volunteer to participate in medical research, especially human challenge trials. It recruited and organized tens of thousands of prospective challenge-trial volunteers during the COVID-19 pandemic and coordinated open letters from scientists and Nobel laureates urging governments to prepare for such trials. Its work has since expanded to challenge studies for hepatitis C, tuberculosis and other infectious diseases, along with broader public health and pandemic-preparedness policy advocacy through affiliated efforts such as 1Day Africa.
justification: Its primary activity is organized public-interest advocacy on biomedical research and public health policy rather than conducting trials or delivering health services itself.

alternates.justification: It is a health-focused voluntary organization mobilizing volunteers around disease research, though it does not primarily raise funds for research.

alternates.naics_title: Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology)
alternates.justification: Staff co-author biomedical research and support challenge-trial study design, but research is secondary to advocacy.
Its framing around research-participant autonomy and rights overlaps with human rights advocacy but is narrower in scope.

category_justification: Wikipedia and nonprofit directories list it as a mission-driven nonprofit advocacy and research organization with no membership base, university affiliation, or government status.

name: ACA International
resolved_name: ACA International, the Association of Credit and Collection Professionals
description: ACA International is a US-based trade association, headquartered in Minnesota, representing companies and professionals in the accounts receivable management, credit and debt collection industry. Its members include collection agencies, creditors, debt buyers, collection law firms and vendors, and the association provides education, certification, compliance resources and industry standards. It also lobbies and files regulatory comments on federal and state legislation affecting debt collection practices.
justification: Its primary activity is operating as a membership trade association promoting the business interests of the credit and collection industry.
category_justification: Its own website and Wikipedia entry describe a dues-paying membership base of collection agencies and creditors whose collective interests it represents.

name: AI Applied Consortium
description: The AI Applied Consortium is a US-based 501(c)(3) organization that connects university researchers with industry partners to apply artificial intelligence, mixed reality and IoT technologies in manufacturing, energy, life sciences and the public sector. It operates a network of specialized labs across the United States and Canada and runs collaborative research projects, workshops and training programs. Its board of trustees draws executives and academics from firms and universities including KPMG, BASF, NVIDIA, Visa, Penn State and DePaul University, and it has formed partnerships such as one with the National Association of Wholesaler-Distributors.
naics_title: Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology)
justification: Its stated core activity is applied AI research and technology development conducted through consortium labs with academic and industry partners.

alternates.justification: The consortium structure and industry partner network resemble a business association advancing shared sector interests.
It delivers AI training workshops and upskilling programs, which is a substantial secondary line of activity.

alternates.naics_title: Other Scientific and Technical Consulting Services
alternates.justification: Its sector-specific AI implementation projects for partner organizations resemble technical consulting engagements.

category_justification: Its website identifies it as a 501(c)(3) whose core work is applied research and training rather than representing members, though the consortium label and industry board leave room for a trade/coalition reading.

name: AI For All Now - aiforallnow.com
description: AI For All Now, branded AIFAN, is a small commercial website and platform based in Hightstown, New Jersey that aggregates news, product listings and research summaries about artificial intelligence. It sells paid AI training sessions across several priced tiers aimed at audiences ranging from beginners to investors. It is operated by a small self-described team and is not affiliated with a university, government body or membership association.
justification: Its only identifiable revenue-generating activity is selling instructor-led AI training sessions to individuals and organizations.

alternates.naics_title: Web Search Portals and All Other Information Services
alternates.justification: The bulk of the site is an aggregated web portal of AI tools, news and research links, which fits an information services portal.
Some of its higher-tier sessions target executives and investors rather than technical users.
It publishes recurring AI news and commentary content, though not in a conventional periodical format.

category_justification: The site is a commercial venture with tiered paid training pricing and a business contact address, with no nonprofit, membership or academic status claimed.

name: AI Progress
description: AI Progress is a US advocacy coalition launched in 2024 that campaigns for copyright and technology policy permitting AI model training on copyrighted material under existing fair use doctrine. Its publicly displayed backers include Amazon, Google, Meta, Microsoft, Anthropic, Cohere, OpenAI and Scale AI. It publishes policy statements, media materials and regulatory comments arguing that new AI-specific copyright restrictions would harm US competitiveness.
justification: It functions as an industry-backed association promoting the shared policy and business interests of AI and technology companies.

alternates.justification: Its output is public policy advocacy campaigning, which fits a general social advocacy organization.
It could be read as a professional body if its participants were individuals rather than corporations.
Its visible activity is largely media and messaging work, though it acts for itself rather than as a paid agency.

category_justification: Its launch announcement describes it explicitly as a coalition, and its site lists named corporate members whose collective policy interests it advances.

name: AI Salon
description: The AI Salon is a community organization founded in San Francisco that convenes discussions about the meaning and societal impact of artificial intelligence. It runs small salon-format gatherings of roughly 10 to 20 people plus larger symposia, having held more than 70 events, and publishes curated summaries through a newsletter. It operates volunteer-run chapters in eight cities including San Francisco, New York, London, Berlin, Bangalore, Lagos, Vancouver and Zurich.
justification: Its primary activity is convening a volunteer-run civic community for public discussion and deliberation about AI rather than selling a service.

alternates.naics_title: Promoters of Performing Arts, Sports, and Similar Events without Facilities
alternates.justification: Its concrete output is organizing and promoting recurring events and symposia without owning venues.
Its stated aim of ensuring civil society input into AI governance shades into public-interest advocacy.

alternates.naics_title: Research and Development in the Social Sciences and Humanities
alternates.justification: It synthesizes and publishes insights from its discussions, though this is documentation rather than formal research.

category_justification: The site presents a volunteer-driven civil-society community with a public-interest mission and no dues-paying membership, commercial offering, or institutional parent, though its legal status is not stated.

name: AI Tennessee
resolved_name: AI Tennessee Initiative, University of Tennessee
description: AI Tennessee is a statewide artificial intelligence initiative led by the University of Tennessee that links higher education, K-12 schools, industry and state government. It runs research and development programs, awards seed grants for applied AI projects, coordinates AI workforce development and internships, and convenes events such as the AI CORE Conference and the AI Tennessee Summit. It also operates the AI TechX industry consortium and draws on regional assets including Oak Ridge National Laboratory and the Tennessee Valley Authority.
justification: It is an initiative housed within and led by the University of Tennessee, whose research, education and workforce activities are university functions.

alternates.naics_title: Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology)
alternates.justification: A large share of the initiative's work is funding and coordinating applied AI research and development.
Its coordination role across K-12, universities and employers resembles educational support rather than direct instruction.
Its workforce upskilling programs for Tennessee employers are a form of professional development training.

category_justification: University of Tennessee news and the initiative's own About page state it is a statewide initiative led by the University of Tennessee, making it a sub-unit of a degree-granting institution.

name: AI2030
description: AI 2030 is a Chicago-headquartered membership organization that describes itself as a global movement mobilizing leaders and institutions toward responsible and beneficial uses of artificial intelligence. Its programs include an accelerator for AI startups, fellowships and leadership certification, research on responsible AI governance, summits and conferences, and local AI councils in cities such as Chicago, Boston and New York. Membership is by application, and the organization is listed in nonprofit directories as a Chicago-based nonprofit.
justification: Its core activity is running an application-based membership network of AI professionals and institutional leaders with fellowships, certification and chapters.

alternates.justification: Its city councils and community-building events resemble a civic membership organization more than a credentialing professional body.
Institutional and corporate members and its startup accelerator suggest a business-interest association.
Its fellowship and leadership certification programs are a substantial professional development training line.

category_justification: Its website runs an apply-to-join membership program and regional councils, making a membership base of professionals and institutions its defining feature.

name: Abnormal Security
description: Abnormal Security (recently branded Abnormal AI) is a privately held US cybersecurity vendor headquartered in San Francisco that sells a cloud-native email and human-behavior security platform. Its software uses behavioral AI models to profile normal user and communication patterns in Microsoft 365 and Google Workspace and to block phishing, business email compromise, and account takeover. The company licenses the platform to enterprise customers on a subscription basis and is an independent venture-backed firm rather than a subsidiary.
justification: Its primary activity is developing and licensing a proprietary security software platform to enterprise customers, which is software publishing rather than consulting or hosting.

alternates.naics_title: Computing Infrastructure Providers, Data Processing, Web Hosting, and Related Services
alternates.justification: The product is delivered as a hosted cloud service that continuously processes customer email data.
The offering includes security system design and integration into customer email environments.
Managed detection and response style security operations could be treated as other computer services.

category_justification: It is a venture-backed for-profit corporation selling commercial software subscriptions.

name: Accolade
description: Accolade, Inc. is a US health benefits and care-delivery company, historically headquartered in Seattle and Plymouth Meeting, Pennsylvania, that contracts with employers and health plans. It combines human care advocates and clinicians with a technology platform to help members navigate benefits, find providers, and access virtual primary care and expert medical opinion services. Formerly publicly traded, it was acquired by Transcarent in 2025 and now operates as part of that company.
naics_title: All Other Miscellaneous Ambulatory Health Care Services
justification: Its primary activity is delivering personalized health advocacy, care navigation, and virtual clinical services to members, which fits miscellaneous ambulatory health care rather than insurance or software.

alternates.naics_title: Pharmacy Benefit Management and Other Third Party Administration of Insurance and Pension Funds
alternates.justification: A large part of the business is administering and steering employer health benefit programs on behalf of plan sponsors.
Its virtual primary care and mental health offerings function as outpatient care delivery.
The member-facing navigation platform is a licensed software product sold to employers.

category_justification: It is a for-profit commercial vendor, formerly NASDAQ-listed, selling services to employer clients.

name: Adaptive Computing Enterprises
description: Adaptive Computing Enterprises, Inc. is a privately held US software company, historically based in Naples, Florida after origins in Provo, Utah, that sells workload and resource management software for high performance computing. Its principal products are the Moab HPC Suite scheduler and the Heidi AI cloud supercomputing platform, used by national laboratories, universities, and enterprises to schedule jobs across clusters. The company is an independent commercial vendor and traces its lineage to the open-source Maui and TORQUE scheduling projects.
justification: The company's primary activity is developing and licensing packaged HPC scheduling and workload management software products.

alternates.justification: It also designs and integrates HPC and AI cluster environments for customers.

alternates.naics_title: Computing Infrastructure Providers, Data Processing, Web Hosting, and Related Services
alternates.justification: Its newer Heidi platform offers hosted cloud supercomputing capacity.
Some revenue comes from custom engineering and support engagements around the scheduler.

category_justification: It is a privately held for-profit corporation selling commercial software licenses and support.

name: Adobe
description: Adobe Inc. is a publicly traded US software company headquartered in San Jose, California. It develops and licenses creative, document, and marketing software including Photoshop, Illustrator, Premiere Pro, Acrobat and the PDF format, and the Adobe Experience Cloud, and has embedded generative AI through its Firefly models. Nearly all revenue comes from subscription licensing of these software products to consumers, creative professionals, and enterprises.
justification: Adobe's overwhelming primary activity is developing and licensing packaged application software, the defining activity of software publishers.
category_justification: It is a NASDAQ-listed for-profit corporation commenting in its own commercial capacity.

name: Advocate Health
description: Advocate Health is a nonprofit integrated health system headquartered in Charlotte, North Carolina, formed by the 2022 combination of Advocate Aurora Health and Atrium Health. It operates dozens of hospitals and roughly a thousand care sites across the Carolinas, Illinois, Wisconsin, Georgia, and Alabama, and is among the largest nonprofit health systems in the United States. It also runs medical education and research operations, including an academic partnership with Wake Forest University School of Medicine.
justification: Its primary activity is operating a large network of acute care general hospitals and associated inpatient services.
category_justification: It is a tax-exempt nonprofit hospital system, not a membership body, university, or government unit.

name: Alignment AI
description: Research could not confirm which entity submitted under the name Alignment AI. Several similarly named organizations exist, including ALIGNMT AI, a Seattle-based AI governance software startup, AlignAI, an enterprise AI enablement vendor, and Aligned AI, a UK AI alignment research company, but none could be tied to this comment. The name is too generic and too close to the common technical term AI alignment to identify a specific organization with confidence.
naics_title: Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology)
justification: If the name denotes an AI alignment research group, computer science research and development would be the fitting code, but the entity itself is unverified.

alternates.justification: Several candidate entities with this name are commercial AI governance or enablement software vendors.

alternates.naics_title: Administrative Management and General Management Consulting Services
alternates.justification: Some similarly named firms operate as AI governance and adoption consultancies.
The name could equally belong to a nonprofit AI safety advocacy group.

category_justification: Web search returned multiple distinct organizations with near-identical names and no evidence linking any of them to this submission.

name: Allen Institue for AI
description: The Allen Institute for AI, branded Ai2, is a nonprofit artificial intelligence research institute in Seattle founded in 2014 by Microsoft co-founder Paul Allen. It conducts and publishes open AI research, releasing open-source models and datasets such as the OLMo language models, Molmo, Semantic Scholar, and AllenNLP. It is an independent 501(c)(3) organization, distinct from but sharing a founder with the Allen Institute for Brain Science, and it also operates an incubator for AI startups.
naics_title: Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology)
justification: Its primary activity is conducting engineering and computer science research and development, which NAICS places in physical and engineering sciences R&D.

alternates.naics_title: Research and Development in the Social Sciences and Humanities
alternates.justification: Part of its work addresses AI policy and societal impact rather than engineering.
It releases widely used open-source software and model artifacts.

alternates.naics_title: Web Search Portals and All Other Information Services
alternates.justification: Its Semantic Scholar product is a public academic search and information service.

category_justification: It is a 501(c)(3) research institute with a public-interest open research mission and no membership base or degree-granting role.

name: Amazon
description: Amazon.com, Inc. is a publicly traded US multinational headquartered in Seattle, Washington. Its largest revenue source is online and physical general merchandise retail, including its first-party stores and third-party marketplace services, alongside advertising and Prime subscriptions. It also operates Amazon Web Services, the cloud computing and AI infrastructure division that supplies most of the company's operating profit, plus devices, logistics, and media businesses.
justification: By revenue, Amazon's primary activity is general merchandise retailing across a broad range of product lines, principally online.

alternates.naics_title: Computing Infrastructure Providers, Data Processing, Web Hosting, and Related Services
alternates.justification: Amazon Web Services is the dominant profit center and a major cloud infrastructure provider.

alternates.naics_title: Corporate, Subsidiary, and Regional Managing Offices
alternates.justification: The named entity is a holding and managing parent over many distinct operating businesses.

alternates.naics_title: Media Streaming Distribution Services, Social Networks, and Other Media Networks and Content Providers
alternates.justification: Prime Video and related media distribution are a significant secondary line.

category_justification: It is a NASDAQ-listed for-profit corporation commenting in its own commercial capacity.

name: American Security Fund
resolved_name: American Security Fund (American Security Fund + Foundation)
description: The American Security Fund is a Washington, DC-based advocacy organization, registered with the IRS as a 501(c)(4) social welfare organization (EIN 30-1365638), that works on artificial intelligence security, safety, and ethics policy. It publishes policy briefs and research, endorses federal legislation such as the People-First Chatbot Act, and convenes events including the Athens Summit on AI Ethics with religious and civic leaders. It operates alongside a companion charitable entity and is presented publicly as the American Security Fund + Foundation.
justification: Its primary activity is issue advocacy and policy promotion on AI safety and ethics rather than service delivery or commerce, which is the core of the social advocacy organization category.

alternates.justification: As a 501(c)(4) that endorses legislation and lobbies, it has some characteristics of a political organization, though it is not an electoral or campaign committee.

alternates.naics_title: Research and Development in the Social Sciences and Humanities
alternates.justification: It produces policy briefs and research findings, which could support a social science research classification if research were its dominant output.
Its convening of summits and leader networks gives it a civic organization character, but advocacy rather than member fellowship is the primary activity.

category_justification: IRS and ProPublica records show a 501(c)(4) tax-exempt entity pursuing a public-interest AI policy mission with no evidence of a dues-paying membership base, so it is a mission-driven nonprofit rather than a membership coalition.

name: Americans for Tax Reform
description: Americans for Tax Reform (ATR) is a Washington, DC-based 501(c)(4) advocacy organization founded in 1985 by Grover Norquist to promote lower, flatter, and simpler taxes and limited government. It is best known for the Taxpayer Protection Pledge, which asks legislators and candidates to commit in writing to oppose tax increases, and it publishes policy analysis and testimony across federal and state issues including technology and AI regulation. It also convenes the weekly Wednesday Meeting, a coordinating forum for center-right organizations, and is affiliated with the Americans for Tax Reform Foundation.
justification: ATR's primary activity is promoting a fiscal and regulatory policy agenda to legislators and the public, which is the defining activity of a social advocacy organization.

alternates.justification: Its candidate pledge program and heavy engagement with elected officials give it political organization characteristics, though it is not a campaign committee or party organ.
Its Wednesday Meeting convening role resembles a civic organization function, but this is secondary to policy advocacy.

alternates.naics_title: Research and Development in the Social Sciences and Humanities
alternates.justification: It produces tax and regulatory policy analysis, which would fit social science research if analysis rather than advocacy were dominant.

category_justification: ATR is a 501(c)(4) mission-driven policy organization with no dues-paying membership base representing members' collective interests, so it falls under nonprofit rather than trade/coalition despite its coalition-convening role.

name: Applied Digital
description: Applied Digital Corporation (Nasdaq: APLD) is a publicly traded, Dallas-based company that designs, builds, and operates large-scale data centers for high-performance computing and artificial intelligence workloads. Its business segments include data center hosting for digital asset customers and purpose-built HPC campuses in North Dakota and other locations leased to AI and cloud tenants. It also offers a cloud services business providing GPU compute capacity to AI customers.
naics_title: Computing Infrastructure Providers, Data Processing, Web Hosting, and Related Services
justification: The company's primary activity is owning and operating data center facilities that provide computing infrastructure, hosting, and GPU compute capacity to customers.
category_justification: It is a for-profit corporation listed on the Nasdaq stock exchange under the ticker APLD.

name: Arch Systems
description: Arch Systems is a Silicon Valley-based, venture-backed software company founded in 2015 by Andrew Scheuermann and Timothy Burke that sells AI and analytics products for manufacturing operations. Its ArchFX platform, including Arch Data Twin, Arch GLO, and Arch AI components, collects and normalizes machine data from factory equipment and delivers process-control and productivity recommendations to electronics manufacturers. The company markets to global electronics and surface-mount technology manufacturers and is not a subsidiary of a larger parent.
justification: Its primary activity is developing and licensing a proprietary manufacturing analytics software platform (ArchFX) to industrial customers.

alternates.justification: Deployment of factory data connectors and edge gateways involves systems integration work that could dominate revenue in some engagements.

alternates.naics_title: Computing Infrastructure Providers, Data Processing, Web Hosting, and Related Services
alternates.justification: The platform is delivered as a cloud service that ingests and processes large volumes of machine data on customers' behalf.

alternates.naics_title: Other Scientific and Technical Consulting Services
alternates.justification: The company advises manufacturers on process improvement, which could be read as technical consulting rather than software supply.

category_justification: Company sources and investor databases describe a for-profit, venture-funded corporation selling commercial software, though the generic name is shared by several firms so the identification carries some residual risk.

name: Atlassian
description: Atlassian is a publicly traded enterprise software company (Nasdaq: TEAM), founded in Australia in 2002 and now domiciled in the United States with major offices in Sydney and San Francisco. It develops and sells collaboration and software-development tools including Jira, Confluence, Bitbucket, Trello, and Jira Service Management, delivered predominantly as cloud subscriptions. Its customers are businesses and government agencies worldwide, and the company operates independently rather than as a subsidiary.
justification: Atlassian's primary activity is designing, publishing, and licensing its own packaged software products to business customers.
category_justification: It is a for-profit corporation publicly listed on the Nasdaq stock exchange under the ticker TEAM.

name: Authors Guild
description: The Authors Guild is a New York-based membership organization for published writers, founded in 1912 and describing itself as the oldest and largest professional organization for writers in the United States. It provides members with contract review, legal assistance, and business resources, and it advocates on copyright, free expression, and fair compensation, including litigation against AI developers over the use of books in model training. It is affiliated with the Authors Guild Foundation, its charitable education arm.
justification: Its primary activity is serving a dues-paying membership of professional writers through advocacy, legal support, and professional services, which is the defining function of a professional organization.

alternates.naics_title: Labor Unions and Similar Labor Organizations
alternates.justification: Its guild structure and work on compensation and contract terms for working writers resembles a labor organization, though it is not a certified collective bargaining unit.
Much of its public activity is copyright and free-expression advocacy, which could support a social advocacy classification.
It maintains a member community with events and programming, a secondary civic-organization characteristic.

category_justification: It is explicitly a dues-based membership body whose stated purpose is representing the collective professional and economic interests of writers.

name: AutogenAI
description: AutogenAI is a for-profit software company founded in 2022 by Sean Williams and headquartered in London, with operations in the United States, Canada, and Australia. It sells a generative AI platform that helps organizations draft, edit, and manage bids, tenders, and grant proposals, using large language models tuned to a client's own content library. The company is venture-backed by investors including Salesforce Ventures, Blossom Capital, and Spark Capital, and operates independently.
justification: Its primary activity is developing and licensing its own proprietary generative AI proposal-writing software to business and government customers on a subscription basis.

alternates.naics_title: Computing Infrastructure Providers, Data Processing, Web Hosting, and Related Services
alternates.justification: The product is delivered as a hosted cloud service that processes customer document data, which could support a data processing classification.
The platform is tuned to each client's language library, which involves customization work that could be read as custom programming.
Client onboarding includes integration and configuration services that resemble systems design engagements.

category_justification: It is a privately held, venture-funded for-profit company selling a commercial software subscription.

name: Basecamp Tech Fest
description: Basecamp Tech Fest is a technology, business, and creative conference based in the Boise, Idaho metropolitan area, which held its inaugural two-day event in Meridian, Idaho in September 2025. It runs three programming tracks (TechCamp, CreativeCamp, and BizCamp) with keynotes, workshops, panels, and networking aimed at both technology builders and general audiences, and emphasizes accessibility features such as ASL interpretation. Its website carries an LLC copyright notice, indicating it is operated as a for-profit event company rather than as a program of a larger institution.
justification: Its primary activity is organizing, promoting, and managing a multi-day conference and exhibition event for technology and business audiences.

alternates.naics_title: Promoters of Performing Arts, Sports, and Similar Events without Facilities
alternates.justification: Its festival framing with staged programming at rented venues could place it among event promoters without their own facilities.
The workshop and skills-track content has a professional development character that could dominate if training were its core product.
Its promotion of the Boise area as a growing tech hub overlaps with destination-promotion activity, though it does not function as a visitors bureau.

category_justification: The event website's LLC designation and ticketed, sponsor-funded festival model indicate a for-profit event business, though no incorporation filing was located to confirm it.

name: BevelCloud
description: BevelCloud is a private U.S. technology company that operates a distributed cloud infrastructure platform for running AI applications at the point of care, such as hospitals, clinics, imaging centers, and ambulances. Rather than moving sensitive medical data to centralized data centers, its platform deploys inference, image-sharing, and federated-learning applications onto compute nodes located where the data already resides, which it presents as a privacy-preserving and low-latency alternative to hyperscale cloud. It also maintains AppCommons, a catalog of healthcare AI research applications packaged for deployment on its infrastructure.
naics_title: Computing Infrastructure Providers, Data Processing, Web Hosting, and Related Services
justification: Its primary activity is providing distributed computing infrastructure and hosting on which third-party AI applications are run, which is the core of 518210.

alternates.justification: It also develops and licenses the platform software layer that packages and deploys AI applications.
Deploying edge compute nodes into hospital IT environments involves systems design and integration work.

alternates.naics_title: Web Search Portals and All Other Information Services
alternates.justification: Its AppCommons catalog is an information/directory service, though secondary to the infrastructure business.

category_justification: It is a venture-backed for-profit vendor selling a commercial cloud platform, with terms of use and paid studio product, not a mission or membership body.

name: BioMADE
resolved_name: BioMADE (Bioindustrial Manufacturing and Design Ecosystem), a Manufacturing USA institute sponsored by the U.S. Department of Defense
description: BioMADE is a nonprofit Manufacturing Innovation Institute established in 2020 with roughly $87 million in initial U.S. Department of Defense funding and operating within the federal Manufacturing USA network. It funds and coordinates research, pilot-scale facilities, and workforce programs intended to build domestic bioindustrial manufacturing capacity and reduce the risk of private investment in biomanufacturing infrastructure. It works through a membership network of companies, universities, and nonprofits, but is itself an independently incorporated organization rather than a federal agency.
naics_title: Research and Development in Biotechnology (except Nanobiotechnology)
justification: Its primary activity is funding, coordinating, and conducting applied biotechnology research and development in bioindustrial manufacturing processes.

alternates.naics_title: Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology)
alternates.justification: Much of its portfolio is process and manufacturing engineering R&D rather than biotechnology proper.
It is organized around a dues-paying member network of firms and institutions in the bioindustrial sector.

alternates.naics_title: Other Similar Organizations (except Business, Professional, Labor, and Political Organizations)
alternates.justification: As a public-private consortium it could be treated as an other similar membership organization.

category_justification: It is an independently incorporated nonprofit institute whose core activity is funding research, pilot facilities, and workforce development rather than advocating for members' collective interests, though its consortium membership model makes trade/coalition a close call.

name: Bleeding Hearts
description: Research could not confirm which entity this name refers to in the context of a U.S. federal AI policy Request for Information. Searches surface several unrelated organizations sharing the name, including a Florida youth-run charity called Bleeding Hearts Across America, a Bleeding Hearts Foundation, a Minneapolis art studio, and small commercial ventures, none of which show any connection to AI policy comment. No public record was found tying any of these to the AI RFI docket, so the submitter's nature and activity remain unverified.
naics_title: Other Similar Organizations (except Business, Professional, Labor, and Political Organizations)
justification: No verified activity was found; this residual membership/other-organization code is a placeholder rather than an evidenced classification.

alternates.justification: If the submitter is the advocacy-style charity of that name, a social advocacy code would apply.
A small volunteer community group of this name would fall under civic and social organizations.
If the submitter is instead a small technology or design shop, a software services code would apply.

category_justification: Multiple distinct unrelated entities share this name and no source links any of them to the AI RFI, so the entity type cannot be confirmed.

name: Boston Dynamics
resolved_name: Boston Dynamics, Inc., a subsidiary of Hyundai Motor Group
description: Boston Dynamics is a Massachusetts-based robotics company that designs, manufactures, and sells mobile robots, including the Spot quadruped, the Stretch warehouse robot, and the humanoid Atlas platform. It combines in-house mechanical hardware production with control software, perception, and increasingly AI-based autonomy for industrial inspection, logistics, and manufacturing customers. Originally a spinoff of MIT research and later owned by Google and SoftBank, it is now majority-owned by Hyundai Motor Group.
naics_title: All Other Miscellaneous General Purpose Machinery Manufacturing
justification: Its primary activity is designing and manufacturing robots for commercial sale, which NAICS places in the all-other general purpose machinery manufacturing category.

alternates.naics_title: Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology)
alternates.justification: A large share of its work is advanced robotics R&D, historically funded by DARPA and corporate parents.

alternates.naics_title: All Other Miscellaneous Electrical Equipment and Component Manufacturing
alternates.justification: Its robots are electrically actuated systems that could be coded under miscellaneous electrical equipment.
It also licenses fleet-management and autonomy software alongside the hardware.

category_justification: It is a for-profit corporate subsidiary of Hyundai Motor Group selling robots commercially.

name: Bright Query
description: BrightQuery is a for-profit U.S. data company that compiles firmographic, financial, employment, and ESG information on more than 30 million public and private American companies. It builds its datasets primarily from official government filings such as IRS, SEC, Department of Labor, SBA, and USPS records, and delivers them through bulk files, APIs, and an online analytics terminal. Its customers use the data for investment analysis, credit and risk assessment, compliance, and competitive intelligence.
naics_title: Web Search Portals and All Other Information Services
justification: Its primary activity is compiling and licensing proprietary business-information databases, which NAICS places among other information services.

alternates.naics_title: Computing Infrastructure Providers, Data Processing, Web Hosting, and Related Services
alternates.justification: Large-scale ingestion and processing of government filings into structured data is a data processing service.
It sells a hosted analytics terminal and APIs that could be treated as licensed software products.
Its company financial and risk data products are used for credit and counterparty assessment.

category_justification: It is a privately held commercial data vendor selling subscription datasets and analytics, with registered trademarks under BrightQuery, Inc.

name: Brightband
description: Brightband is a venture-backed San Francisco startup founded in 2024 that develops AI and machine-learning models for weather and climate forecasting. It trains models on public observational and reanalysis data and aims to release open-source models and datasets while commercializing forecast products and services for sectors such as energy, insurance, agriculture, and aviation. It was founded by former Google and technology-industry executives and positions itself as an alternative to legacy numerical weather prediction pipelines.
naics_title: All Other Professional, Scientific, and Technical Services
justification: Weather forecasting services are classified in NAICS under all other professional, scientific, and technical services, and delivering forecasts is the company's core output.

alternates.justification: It develops and distributes forecasting models and software, including open-source releases, as its main technical product.

alternates.naics_title: Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology)
alternates.justification: As an early-stage company its work is still largely atmospheric-science and ML research and development.

alternates.naics_title: Computing Infrastructure Providers, Data Processing, Web Hosting, and Related Services
alternates.justification: It processes and hosts large meteorological datasets and serves forecasts through APIs.

category_justification: It is a for-profit venture-funded startup that has raised institutional capital to commercialize forecasting products.

name: Brooklyn Law Incubator & Policy Clinic
resolved_name: Brooklyn Law Incubator & Policy Clinic (BLIP), Brooklyn Law School
description: The Brooklyn Law Incubator & Policy Clinic, known as BLIP, is a clinical legal education program at Brooklyn Law School founded and directed by professor Jonathan Askin. Enrolled law students, supervised by faculty, provide pro bono transactional and intellectual property legal services to early-stage technology startups and nonprofits while also producing advocacy and comment filings on internet, telecommunications, and technology policy. It operates as a teaching unit of Brooklyn Law School rather than as an independent legal or advocacy entity.
justification: It is an in-house clinical teaching program of a professional law school, so its primary activity is degree-granting professional education.

alternates.justification: Its day-to-day output is supervised legal representation of startup and nonprofit clients.
Clinic work includes non-attorney legal support and policy drafting that falls outside conventional law offices.
The policy side of the clinic files public-interest advocacy comments in technology proceedings.

category_justification: BLIP is a curricular clinic housed within and staffed by Brooklyn Law School, a degree-granting professional school, not a separately incorporated organization.

name: COGR
description: The Council on Governmental Relations is a Washington, D.C. based association founded in 1948 that represents more than 140 research-intensive U.S. universities and affiliated research foundations. It analyzes federal regulations and policies affecting sponsored research, engages federal agencies on compliance and cost-recovery issues, and works to reduce administrative burden on member institutions. Membership is restricted to institutions meeting defined research and graduate education criteria, and the organization operates through a board and standing committees.
justification: Its primary activity is operating a dues-based association that represents the collective regulatory and policy interests of member research institutions.

alternates.justification: Its constituency is research administration professionals and it publishes professional guidance and best practices.
A substantial share of its work is federal policy advocacy on research regulation.

alternates.naics_title: Research and Development in the Social Sciences and Humanities
alternates.justification: It produces policy analyses and surveys on research administration and federal cost policy.

category_justification: It is an institutional membership association of 140+ universities whose stated purpose is representing those members before federal agencies.

name: Cambio Digital Transformations
description: Cambio Digital Transformations, LLC is a small consulting firm founded by former U.S. Department of Commerce CIO Simon Szykman that serves federal government agencies. It provides digital transformation advisory work, IT and technology strategy, human-centered design, and customer experience services to help agencies modernize their systems and service delivery. It is an SBA-certified woman-owned small business and an active federal contractor (UEI RF8CGEK78DY4, CAGE 9XEK8).
justification: Its primary activity is advising federal agencies on IT modernization and digital/technology transformation, which is planning and design of computer systems rather than general business management consulting.

alternates.naics_title: Administrative Management and General Management Consulting Services
alternates.justification: Much of the work is strategy, organizational change, and management advisory rather than technical systems design.
Customer experience and service-delivery consulting can fall under other specialized management consulting.
Applies only if the firm's delivery work is primarily custom software development for agency clients.

category_justification: It is a for-profit LLC and SBA-certified woman-owned small business registered as a federal contractor, i.e., a professional-services firm operating commercially.

name: Campus Research Computing Consortium
description: The Campus Research Computing Consortium (CaRCC) is a community-led membership organization of research computing and data (RCD) professionals at academic, government, and nonprofit institutions. It runs working groups, a multi-track "People Network," and career-development and capability-maturity programs to advance the RCD profession and institutional research computing capacity. It has been moving toward independent 501(c)(3) status and works closely with Internet2, several of whose staff hold CaRCC leadership roles.
justification: Its primary activity is convening and promoting the interests and professional development of research computing and data practitioners, which is the defining function of a professional membership organization.

alternates.justification: It functions as a voluntary community of practice rather than a formal credentialing body.
A large share of its output is training, curricula, and capability-maturity support for institutional staff.
It explicitly advocates for recognition and funding of the RCD profession and cyberinfrastructure.

category_justification: It is an institution- and practitioner-membership consortium whose stated purpose is advocating for and advancing the shared interests of research computing professionals.

name: Cara
description: Research could not confirm which entity named "Cara" submitted this comment; the name appears without any qualifier. The two leading candidates are Cara (cara.app), a for-profit artist social and portfolio platform founded by photographer Jingna Zhang that bars AI-generated work and applies NoAI tags, and Cara Collective, a Chicago-based nonprofit workforce-development organization. No submission record was located that distinguishes between them or rules out an unrelated entity or individual.
naics_title: Media Streaming Distribution Services, Social Networks, and Other Media Networks and Content Providers
justification: If the commenter is the cara.app artist platform, its primary activity is operating a social network and content-sharing site, but the entity itself is unconfirmed.

alternates.naics_title: Web Search Portals and All Other Information Services
alternates.justification: An online portfolio/discovery portal for artists could be coded as an other information service.
If the commenter is Cara Collective, its primary activity is employment training and job placement for people facing barriers to work.
Applies if the entity is primarily a mobile/web application publisher rather than a network operator.

category_justification: At least two distinct real organizations use the bare name "Cara" - one for-profit platform and one nonprofit - and nothing in the record identifies which one, so the entity type cannot be confirmed.

name: Care New England Health System
description: Care New England Health System is a nonprofit integrated health system headquartered in Providence, Rhode Island, and one of the state's two largest hospital groups. Its member institutions include Women & Infants Hospital, Kent Hospital, Butler Hospital, and The Providence Center, along with affiliated physician practices and home health services. It is a major academic affiliate of the Warren Alpert Medical School of Brown University.
justification: The system's primary activity is operating acute-care hospitals providing general inpatient medical and surgical services, with Kent Hospital as a general acute-care anchor.

alternates.naics_title: Specialty (except Psychiatric and Substance Abuse) Hospitals
alternates.justification: Women & Infants Hospital is a specialty obstetric and newborn hospital and a large share of system volume.
Butler Hospital is a freestanding psychiatric hospital within the system.
The system also runs substantial outpatient behavioral health and ambulatory care operations.

category_justification: It is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit hospital system (EIN 05-0490997) delivering health services, which the instructions place under nonprofit rather than business.

name: Cisco
description: Cisco Systems, Inc. is a publicly traded American technology company headquartered in San Jose, California, and the world's largest maker of enterprise networking equipment. It designs and sells routers, switches, wireless and optical networking hardware, along with cybersecurity, collaboration, observability, and network software and subscription services. It also operates a large services and support business and has expanded into AI infrastructure networking.
justification: Its largest revenue source is designing and manufacturing network communications equipment such as routers and switches, which NAICS classifies under telephone apparatus manufacturing.

alternates.justification: Some of its communications hardware lines fall outside the wired telephone apparatus definition.
A rapidly growing share of revenue is software and security subscriptions such as Splunk, Duo, and Meraki.

alternates.naics_title: Radio and Television Broadcasting and Wireless Communications Equipment Manufacturing
alternates.justification: Its wireless access point and Wi-Fi product lines are wireless communications equipment.

category_justification: Cisco is a publicly traded for-profit corporation (NASDAQ: CSCO) commenting as a commercial technology vendor.

name: City of Hope
description: City of Hope is a nonprofit cancer research and treatment organization headquartered in Duarte, California, and an NCI-designated Comprehensive Cancer Center. It operates City of Hope National Medical Center, the Beckman Research Institute, a graduate school of biological sciences, and a national network of cancer treatment sites including the former Cancer Treatment Centers of America facilities. Its work spans clinical oncology care, hematology and transplant medicine, and translational research in areas such as immunotherapy and diabetes.
naics_title: Specialty (except Psychiatric and Substance Abuse) Hospitals
justification: Its primary activity is operating a specialty cancer hospital and affiliated oncology treatment centers, which is the dominant share of its operations and revenue.

alternates.naics_title: Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology)
alternates.justification: The Beckman Research Institute makes biomedical research a very large secondary activity.
City of Hope National Medical Center provides broad inpatient medical and surgical services beyond oncology.

alternates.naics_title: Research and Development in Biotechnology (except Nanobiotechnology)
alternates.justification: Much of its research pipeline is biotechnology-based, including cell and gene therapies.

category_justification: It is a 501(c)(3) charitable medical and research organization, not a government unit, university, or membership body, despite operating a degree-granting graduate school as a sub-unit.

name: CivicAI Security Program
description: Civic AI Security Program, Inc., known as CivAI, is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit based in Berkeley, California, founded in 2023 by Lucas Hansen and Siddharth Hiregowdara. It raises awareness of AI capabilities and risks through interactive demonstrations of harms such as deepfakes, spear-phishing, and election misinformation, delivered to lawmakers, agencies, and civil society groups. It is a member of the NIST AI consortium and provides private briefings on higher-risk capabilities while declining to endorse specific bills.
justification: Its primary activity is public-interest education and advocacy aimed at shaping awareness and policy around AI risks, which fits other social advocacy organizations.

alternates.justification: Its core deliverable is instructional demonstrations and briefings, a form of educational service.

alternates.naics_title: Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology)
alternates.justification: Building live attack demonstrations involves applied technical research into AI capabilities.
It could be treated as a civic organization convening stakeholders around a public issue.

category_justification: It is an incorporated 501(c)(3) (EIN 93-4182617) pursuing a public-interest mission with no membership base and no government or university affiliation.

name: Click Therapeutics
description: Click Therapeutics, Inc. is a privately held New York City biotechnology company that develops prescription digital therapeutics, which it markets as software as prescription medical treatments. It builds and clinically tests smartphone-based cognitive and behavioral interventions for conditions such as major depressive disorder, schizophrenia, and migraine, and partners with pharmaceutical firms including Boehringer Ingelheim and Otsuka. It is backed by investors including H.I.G. Capital and is a member of the Digital Therapeutics Alliance.
justification: Its products are proprietary therapeutic software applications that it develops, licenses, and distributes, which is the defining activity of a software publisher.

alternates.naics_title: Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology)
alternates.justification: A large share of its operations is running randomized clinical trials to secure FDA authorization.

alternates.naics_title: Research and Development in Biotechnology (except Nanobiotechnology)
alternates.justification: It positions itself as a biotechnology company developing therapeutics under a drug-development model.
Its software-enhanced drug offerings are co-developed with and packaged alongside pharmaceutical products.

category_justification: It is a venture- and private-equity-backed for-profit corporation selling commercial therapeutic products.

name: Cohere
description: Cohere is a privately held artificial intelligence company founded in 2019 and headquartered in Toronto, Canada, with additional offices in San Francisco, New York, and London. It develops proprietary large language, embedding, and retrieval models that it licenses to enterprises through an API and through private deployments on customer or cloud infrastructure. Its offerings include the Command family of models and the North enterprise productivity platform, and it operates as an independent company rather than a subsidiary.
justification: Cohere's primary commercial activity is developing and licensing proprietary AI model software to enterprise customers, which is software publishing rather than a service or hardware business.

alternates.naics_title: Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology)
alternates.justification: A large share of Cohere's activity is frontier model research, which could be treated as engineering and computer science R&D.

alternates.naics_title: Computing Infrastructure Providers, Data Processing, Web Hosting, and Related Services
alternates.justification: Models are delivered as a hosted API service running on managed computing infrastructure.
Cohere does custom fine-tuning and private deployment engineering for individual enterprise clients.

category_justification: Cohere is a venture-backed for-profit corporation selling AI model products to paying enterprise customers.

name: Corewell Health
description: Corewell Health is a not-for-profit integrated health system headquartered in Grand Rapids and Southfield, Michigan, formed in February 2022 by the merger of Spectrum Health and Beaumont Health. It operates more than twenty hospitals along with outpatient sites and a large employed physician group, and it owns the Priority Health insurance plan. It is an independent nonprofit corporation and one of Michigan's largest employers rather than a unit of a larger system.
justification: The system's dominant activity by revenue and staffing is operating general acute-care hospitals across Michigan, with physician offices and a health plan as secondary lines.

alternates.naics_title: Offices of Physicians (except Mental Health Specialists)
alternates.justification: Corewell operates a very large employed medical group delivering ambulatory physician services.

alternates.naics_title: Direct Health and Medical Insurance Carriers
alternates.justification: Its Priority Health subsidiary is a substantial health insurance carrier covering roughly 1.3 million members.
The system runs an extensive network of outpatient and ambulatory care centers.

category_justification: Corewell Health is a 501(c)(3) charitable health system with IRS Form 990 filings and no membership or governmental basis.

name: Cost Quest Associates
description: CostQuest Associates is a for-profit, employee-owned broadband consulting, data, and technology firm with offices in Cincinnati, Ohio and Seattle, Washington. It performs telecommunications network cost modeling, broadband mapping, regulatory policy analysis, and financial advisory work for carriers, state and local governments, and federal agencies. It built and licenses the Broadband Serviceable Location Fabric that underpins the FCC's Broadband Data Collection and NTIA's BEAD program, along with the VerraV mapping and GrantLight grant-compliance tools.
justification: The firm self-describes as a broadband consulting firm and its core revenue activity is telecommunications cost-modeling and regulatory advisory consulting, which falls under telecommunications and utilities management consulting.

alternates.naics_title: Other Scientific and Technical Consulting Services
alternates.justification: Its engineering-economic network cost models and geospatial methodology are technical rather than general management consulting.

alternates.naics_title: Web Search Portals and All Other Information Services
alternates.justification: A major line of business is compiling and licensing the proprietary Broadband Fabric location dataset.

alternates.naics_title: Computing Infrastructure Providers, Data Processing, Web Hosting, and Related Services
alternates.justification: It processes and delivers large-scale location and service data through hosted platforms such as VerraV and GrantLight.

category_justification: CostQuest states on its own site that it is a for-profit, employee-owned firm serving paying commercial and government clients.

name: Credo
description: Credo AI is a for-profit software company founded in 2020 and headquartered in Palo Alto, California, that sells an enterprise AI governance platform. Its software lets organizations inventory AI systems, measure and monitor AI risk, and generate compliance artifacts mapped to frameworks such as the NIST AI Risk Management Framework and the EU AI Act. It is an independent venture-backed company rather than a subsidiary, and its RFI submission identifies it by that name and mission.
justification: Credo AI's primary activity is developing and licensing a packaged AI governance software platform to enterprise and government customers.

alternates.justification: Deployments often involve configuration and integration work tailored to a client's AI systems.

alternates.naics_title: Computing Infrastructure Providers, Data Processing, Web Hosting, and Related Services
alternates.justification: The platform is delivered as a hosted software-as-a-service offering.
The company also advises enterprises on AI risk and compliance program design.

category_justification: The submission's own 'About Credo AI' section describes a venture-funded enterprise software vendor serving Global 2000 and SME customers.

name: Cunningham Concept Design
description: Cunningham Concept Design is a Los Angeles-based design studio led by American industrial designer Matthew Cunningham and presented online at mrcid.com. Its work spans advanced vehicle design, brand futuring for automotive companies such as Toyota and BMW, and concept design of vehicles, props, and sets for feature films and television including Star Trek: Picard, Westworld, Godzilla, and Aquaman. It appears to be a small independent practice built around its principal rather than a division of a larger design or studio organization.
justification: The studio's primary activity is fee-based industrial and concept design of vehicles, products, and physical objects for corporate and entertainment clients.

alternates.justification: Much of the deliverable output is illustration and visual concept art rather than manufacturable product design.

alternates.naics_title: All Other Professional, Scientific, and Technical Services
alternates.justification: Brand futuring and speculative design consulting do not map cleanly to a single named design service code.
A large share of the portfolio is production design work performed for feature films and television series.

category_justification: The commenter is named as a commercial design studio with corporate and film-studio clients, though it is effectively a sole-practitioner for-profit practice.

name: DIGITALEUROPE
description: DIGITALEUROPE is a Brussels-based trade association that represents the digital technology industry in Europe. Its membership combines roughly 100 corporate members, including major hardware, software, semiconductor, and telecommunications firms, with about 40 national digital-technology trade associations from across Europe. It advocates before EU institutions and international bodies on policy areas such as digital trade, data, cybersecurity, and artificial intelligence, and is an independent association rather than a unit of a larger organization.
justification: Its sole activity is representing the collective policy interests of dues-paying corporate and national association members, the defining function of a business association.
category_justification: It publishes a membership roster of corporate members and national trade associations and exists to advance their shared policy positions.

name: Darktrace
description: Darktrace is a cybersecurity company founded in 2013 and headquartered in Cambridge, United Kingdom, with substantial US operations. It develops and sells self-learning artificial intelligence software that detects, investigates, and autonomously responds to cyber threats across network, cloud, email, endpoint, and operational technology environments. Formerly listed on the London Stock Exchange, it was acquired by private equity firm Thoma Bravo in October 2024 and now operates as a Thoma Bravo portfolio company.
justification: Darktrace's primary activity is developing and licensing packaged AI-based cybersecurity software products to enterprise and government customers.

alternates.justification: Deployment involves designing and integrating monitoring appliances and sensors into customer network architectures.

alternates.naics_title: Computing Infrastructure Providers, Data Processing, Web Hosting, and Related Services
alternates.justification: Much of the product is delivered as a cloud-hosted service that ingests and processes customer telemetry.
Its managed detection and incident response offerings are computer-related services rather than product sales.

category_justification: Darktrace is a for-profit commercial software vendor, formerly publicly traded and now privately held by Thoma Bravo.

name: Data Direct Networks
description: DataDirect Networks, commonly branded DDN, is a privately held American company headquartered in Chatsworth, California, that supplies high-performance data storage for high-performance computing and artificial intelligence workloads. It designs and manufactures parallel file system storage appliances and platforms, including the EXAScaler and Infinia lines, sold to national laboratories, research institutions, and enterprises building large AI training and inference infrastructure. It also owns the Tintri and Nexenta storage businesses as subsidiaries.
justification: DDN's primary activity is designing and producing high-performance storage arrays and appliances, which is computer storage device manufacturing.

alternates.justification: A large share of its value and revenue comes from the EXAScaler, Infinia, and Tintri storage software stacks.
It designs and integrates complete storage and data-platform systems for AI and HPC customers.

alternates.naics_title: Computer and Computer Peripheral Equipment and Software Merchant Wholesalers
alternates.justification: Hardware assembly is partly outsourced and much product reaches customers through distribution and OEM channels.

category_justification: DDN is a privately held for-profit technology manufacturer selling storage products commercially.

name: Data Quality Campaign
description: The Data Quality Campaign is a Washington, DC-based national nonprofit founded in 2005 that advocates for the effective and responsible use of education and workforce data. It publishes policy frameworks, state-by-state analyses such as its report card reviews, and guidance for policymakers, educators, and families on data privacy, transparency, and longitudinal data systems. It is an independent 501(c)(3) organization rather than a unit of a larger institution, having begun as a funder-backed collaborative before incorporating on its own.
justification: Its primary activity is issue advocacy and policy campaigning directed at state and federal education data policy, which fits other social advocacy organizations.

alternates.naics_title: Research and Development in the Social Sciences and Humanities
alternates.justification: A substantial share of its output is applied policy research and analysis of state education data systems.
It convenes state agencies and civic stakeholders around shared data-use goals.
It provides technical assistance and implementation guidance to state education agencies.

category_justification: GuideStar and its own about page identify it as an independent 501(c)(3) mission-driven policy organization with no membership base.

name: Davidson Kempner Capital Management
description: Davidson Kempner Capital Management LP is a global institutional alternative investment management firm founded in 1983 and headquartered at 520 Madison Avenue in New York City. It manages roughly $36 billion across event-driven, credit, equity, and real-asset strategies using a bottom-up fundamental approach, with offices in London, Dublin, Hong Kong, Philadelphia, Shenzhen, and Mumbai. It is an SEC-registered investment adviser and an independent partnership rather than a subsidiary of a larger group.
justification: Its primary activity is managing investment portfolios and advising pooled investment vehicles for institutional clients as a registered investment adviser.

alternates.justification: The funds it operates are themselves pooled investment vehicles that could be coded separately from the management company.
Its multi-strategy and real-asset activities span investment services not neatly captured by portfolio management alone.
Event-driven and distressed credit work involves principal trading and intermediation in illiquid instruments.

category_justification: It is a for-profit limited partnership registered with the SEC as an investment adviser and earning management and performance fees.

name: Dcode
description: Dcode is a for-profit government technology firm founded in 2015 and based in Washington, DC that connects commercial technology companies to federal buyers. It runs accelerator cohorts that coach emerging vendors through federal acquisition, sells advisory and training services to government agencies under its own contract vehicles, and operates an affiliated venture fund, Dcode Capital, launched in 2022. It is an independent company rather than a unit of a larger organization.
naics_title: Administrative Management and General Management Consulting Services
justification: Its predominant revenue activity is advisory and go-to-market consulting for technology companies and federal agencies rather than building products or investing.

alternates.justification: Much of the work is specialized federal market-entry and acquisition strategy consulting.
Its accelerator cohorts and agency programs are structured professional training curricula.
Dcode Capital makes venture investments in defense and government technology companies.

category_justification: Its own site states it operates as a for-profit entity earning revenue from government contracts and venture returns.

name: Decision Zone USA
resolved_name: Decision Zone USA (US arm of Decision-Zone Inc., Richmond Hill, Ontario)
description: Decision Zone USA is the United States presence of Decision-Zone Inc., a privately held company founded in 2006 and headquartered in Richmond Hill, Ontario, Canada. Its product is an embedded verification architecture that models the expected message and process behavior of operational systems and deterministically flags any deviation, marketed for cybersecurity of mission-critical and industrial IoT environments. The company is privately funded with no outside institutional backing and licenses its toolset to enterprise and government customers.
justification: Its primary activity is developing and licensing a proprietary security software toolset that customers embed in their systems.

alternates.justification: Deploying the verification architecture requires modeling and integrating into each customer's specific system design.
Ongoing behavioral monitoring and alerting could be treated as a computer-related security service.

alternates.naics_title: Other Scientific and Technical Consulting Services
alternates.justification: The US arm may function largely as technical advisory and business development for the Canadian parent.

category_justification: PitchBook records it as a privately held for-profit corporation selling commercial cybersecurity software.

name: Domelabs AI
description: Domelabs AI is a privately held US company that helps large regulated organizations adopt and govern artificial intelligence. It sells advisory engagements together with supporting technology aimed at moving clients from AI experimentation to governed production use while managing compliance and risk. Its stated customers include federal agencies, Fortune 500 companies, and academic medical centers, and it operates as an independent firm rather than a subsidiary.
naics_title: Administrative Management and General Management Consulting Services
justification: Its lead offering is advisory work on AI governance, policy, and organizational adoption, which is management consulting rather than product development.

alternates.justification: It also designs and implements AI systems and governance tooling inside client environments.
AI risk and regulatory-compliance advisory is a specialized consulting niche rather than general management consulting.
The company markets a governance technology platform alongside its services.

category_justification: It is a commercial vendor selling advisory and technology engagements to enterprise and federal clients for a fee.

name: Dreadnode
description: Dreadnode is a venture-backed US startup that builds AI infrastructure and tooling for offensive security, raising a $14 million Series A in 2025. Its platform lets security teams create, run, and measure autonomous AI agents that stress-test and attack systems and AI models, and it publishes open-source benchmarks on the AI offense-defense gap. It is an independent company whose customers include commercial enterprises and US government and defense organizations.
justification: Its primary activity is developing and licensing a proprietary software platform for building and evaluating offensive security AI agents.

alternates.naics_title: Computing Infrastructure Providers, Data Processing, Web Hosting, and Related Services
alternates.justification: The platform is delivered as hosted infrastructure that runs and orchestrates agent workloads for customers.
Red-teaming and security assessment engagements are computer-related services rather than product sales.

alternates.naics_title: Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology)
alternates.justification: It conducts and publishes original AI security research and benchmark development.

category_justification: It is a for-profit venture-funded startup that announced a $14 million Series A and sells to commercial and government customers.

name: Duke Energy
description: Duke Energy Corporation is a publicly traded US energy holding company headquartered in Charlotte, North Carolina and listed on the NYSE as DUK. Through regulated subsidiaries it generates, transmits, and distributes electricity to roughly 8.6 million customers in the Carolinas, Florida, Indiana, Ohio, and Kentucky, and distributes natural gas in the Carolinas, Ohio, Kentucky, and Tennessee. Its generation fleet spans nuclear, natural gas, coal, hydro, solar, and wind, and it files integrated resource plans with state utility commissions.
justification: The consolidated enterprise's dominant activity is regulated retail electric distribution to millions of end-use customers across six states.

alternates.justification: A large share of its owned capacity and output comes from natural gas and coal generating stations.
The named parent entity is legally a holding company whose operations sit in subsidiary utilities.
It operates one of the largest regulated nuclear fleets in the United States in the Carolinas.

category_justification: It is an investor-owned, NYSE-listed for-profit corporation, not a public power authority.

name: ECRI
resolved_name: ECRI (formerly ECRI Institute; parent of the Institute for Safe Medication Practices)
description: ECRI is an independent nonprofit healthcare research organization founded in 1968 and headquartered in Plymouth Meeting, Pennsylvania, with roughly 550 staff worldwide. It performs independent comparative laboratory evaluation and testing of medical devices, conducts evidence-based health technology assessment as a designated AHRQ Evidence-based Practice Center, investigates device-related incidents, and maintains the Universal Medical Device Nomenclature System. The Institute for Safe Medication Practices became an ECRI affiliate in 2020, and ECRI sells subscription advisory and safety programs to hospitals and health systems.
justification: Its defining primary activity is independent laboratory testing and comparative evaluation of medical devices and technologies for safety and performance.

alternates.naics_title: Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology)
alternates.justification: It operates as an AHRQ Evidence-based Practice Center producing systematic reviews and applied health technology research.

alternates.naics_title: Other Scientific and Technical Consulting Services
alternates.justification: Much of its revenue comes from technical safety and technology-management advisory subscriptions sold to health systems.

alternates.naics_title: Web Search Portals and All Other Information Services
alternates.justification: It publishes and licenses databases such as UMDNS and its guidelines and alerts libraries.

category_justification: It is a long-established independent 501(c)(3) research organization with a public-interest patient safety mission and no membership governance.

name: Marta Ali Studios
description: Marta Ali Studios is a Baltimore, Maryland-based multidisciplinary design and fabrication firm founded by designer Marta Ali. It offers architectural and industrial design, set and exhibit design, computational and multimedia design, and advanced manufacturing and prototyping services including 3D printing, serving building, entertainment, hospitality, government, and fashion clients. In its RFI submission it describes itself as an innovative design and fabrication company working across the building and manufacturing sectors and promotes AI adoption through its 'Designing the Future Now' initiative.
justification: The firm's primary activity is providing custom multidisciplinary design services (architectural, set, computational, and product design) that do not fall cleanly into architectural, interior, or graphic design, which is what Other Specialized Design Services covers.

alternates.justification: The studio does product and prototype design paired with advanced manufacturing, a core industrial design activity.
It lists architectural design and construction management for building projects among its lead services.
It is listed on manufacturing directories as a 3D-printing fabricator producing custom physical goods.

category_justification: It is a for-profit design and fabrication company with commercial clients, and the NITRD respondent index labels it 'Private sector'.

name: Massive Bio
description: Massive Bio is a New York-based for-profit health technology company that operates an AI-driven platform matching cancer patients to clinical trials. Its SYNERGY-AI system ingests patient records and pairs them with eligible oncology trials, supported by concierge navigation services for patients and enrollment services for sponsors. Revenue comes from partnerships with pharmaceutical companies, contract research organizations, and research institutions rather than from patients.
naics_title: Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology)
justification: Its primary revenue activity is providing clinical-trial patient identification and enrollment services to pharmaceutical sponsors and CROs, a contract clinical research service classified in 541715.

alternates.justification: The company describes itself as an AI technology platform and distributes patient-facing web and mobile applications.

alternates.naics_title: All Other Miscellaneous Ambulatory Health Care Services
alternates.justification: Its patient navigation and trial-matching support functions resemble a non-clinical ambulatory health service.
Much of the work is building and tailoring AI matching software for partner institutions.

category_justification: It is a venture-backed for-profit corporation selling services to pharmaceutical and CRO customers, and the NITRD index labels it 'Private sector'.

name: Mathematica
