description: Mathematica Inc. is an employee-owned, for-profit research and consulting firm headquartered in Princeton, New Jersey, formerly known as Mathematica Policy Research. It conducts program evaluation, policy analysis, survey research, data science, and technology work for federal, state, and foundation clients across health, education, disability, labor, and international development. It employed roughly 1,900 staff and reported about $266 million in revenue in 2024.
naics_title: Research and Development in the Social Sciences and Humanities
justification: Its primary activity is contract social-policy research and program evaluation, the defining service of R&D in the social sciences.

alternates.naics_title: Administrative Management and General Management Consulting Services
alternates.justification: A large share of its work is advisory consulting to government program administrators.

alternates.naics_title: Marketing Research and Public Opinion Polling
alternates.justification: It runs large-scale survey design and data collection operations.

alternates.naics_title: Other Scientific and Technical Consulting Services
alternates.justification: It provides technical assistance and data-systems advice alongside its research.

category_justification: Mathematica is a for-profit ESOP employee-owned corporation selling research services under contract, despite the NITRD index labeling it 'Non-profit'.

name: MetaEthics AI
description: MetaEthics AI is a small limited liability company registered in Bountiful, Utah, that works on ethics frameworks for artificial intelligence systems. In its RFI submission it states that its mission is to develop ethically grounded AI systems informed by philosophical frameworks, historical insights, and continuous societal feedback. It promotes a proprietary approach it calls Social Functional Categorization Theory, an adaptive framework intended to quantify AI's societal impact and feed into international AI standards work.
naics_title: Research and Development in the Social Sciences and Humanities
justification: Its identifiable output is a philosophy- and social-science-based evaluation framework for measuring AI's societal effects, which is research in the social sciences and humanities.

alternates.naics_title: Other Scientific and Technical Consulting Services
alternates.justification: It positions itself as advising developers and standards bodies on AI ethics evaluation methods.

alternates.naics_title: Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology)
alternates.justification: It claims to develop AI systems, which would be engineering research and development.
If its ethics scorecards are delivered as a commercial software product, software publishing would apply.

category_justification: State business records list it as Metaethics AI LLC, a for-profit limited liability company, rather than the 'Non-profit' the NITRD index reports.

name: Metrify Health
description: Metrify Health is a small early-stage US health technology venture associated with founder John Kim. Its RFI submission describes three years of work building an AI-enabled precision education platform tailored to nurse practitioner training, combining didactic content, simulation, and clinical-rotation support. The stated customers are academic NP programs, health systems, and insurers, with the goal of expanding primary care capacity in underserved and rural communities.
justification: Its primary activity is developing and offering an AI-enabled educational software platform as a product to nurse practitioner training programs and health systems.

alternates.justification: The platform functions as instructional support and curriculum services for NP degree programs rather than as a standalone software license.
An early-stage venture of this size may principally be building custom software for individual institutional clients.
If it delivers the clinical training content directly to learners it would be a technical training provider.

category_justification: It presents as a named commercial health-tech venture with its own product and website, not a membership body, contradicting the NITRD index label of 'Industry/professional/scientific association'.

name: MistralAI
description: Mistral AI is a Paris-based artificial intelligence company founded in 2023 by former Google DeepMind and Meta researchers. It develops large language models and multimodal AI systems, releasing some as open-weight models and selling others through its commercial API platform, enterprise deployments, and the Le Chat assistant. It is one of the largest European AI model developers and competes with US frontier labs.
justification: Its primary activity is developing and distributing AI models and assistant software products to businesses and consumers, which is software publishing.

alternates.naics_title: Computing Infrastructure Providers, Data Processing, Web Hosting, and Related Services
alternates.justification: Much of its revenue comes from hosted model inference delivered through its API platform.

alternates.naics_title: Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology)
alternates.justification: It operates as a frontier research lab producing novel model architectures.
It performs bespoke model customization and deployment engagements for enterprise and government clients.

category_justification: Mistral AI is a venture-funded for-profit company selling AI products commercially, and the NITRD index labels it 'Private sector'.

name: Modine Manufacturing
description: Modine Manufacturing Company is a publicly traded thermal management manufacturer headquartered in Racine, Wisconsin, listed on the NYSE as MOD. Its Climate Solutions segment makes data center cooling systems, heat pumps, commercial and industrial HVAC equipment, and heat transfer products, including the Airedale by Modine product line. Its Performance Technologies segment supplies heat exchangers and thermal components for vehicles and off-highway equipment.
naics_title: Air-Conditioning and Warm Air Heating Equipment and Commercial and Industrial Refrigeration Equipment Manufacturing
justification: Its largest segment manufactures air-conditioning, data center cooling, and commercial heating equipment, placing its primary activity in 333415.

alternates.justification: Its Performance Technologies segment historically built vehicular radiators and heat exchangers as automotive parts.

alternates.naics_title: Heating Equipment (except Warm Air Furnaces) Manufacturing
alternates.justification: It manufactures unit heaters and hydronic heating products that fall under this heating equipment code.

alternates.naics_title: Industrial and Commercial Fan and Blower and Air Purification Equipment Manufacturing
alternates.justification: Its data center cooling units incorporate large fan, blower, and air handling assemblies.

category_justification: It is a publicly traded for-profit manufacturer (NYSE: MOD), and the NITRD index labels it 'Private sector'.

name: Mount Sinai Health System
description: Mount Sinai Health System is a nonprofit academic health system in New York City formed by the 2013 merger of Mount Sinai Medical Center and Continuum Health Partners. It operates eight hospital campuses, including The Mount Sinai Hospital, along with ambulatory practices and outpatient centers across the metropolitan area. Its academic partner is the Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai, which conducts biomedical research and trains physicians and scientists.
justification: Its primary activity is operating general medical and surgical hospitals providing inpatient acute care across eight campuses.
category_justification: It is a tax-exempt nonprofit hospital system delivering patient care rather than a university, membership body, or government unit, consistent with the NITRD index label 'Non-profit'.

name: Mozilla
resolved_name: Mozilla (Mozilla Foundation and its wholly owned subsidiary Mozilla Corporation)
description: Mozilla is an open-source internet organization founded in 1998 that consists of the non-profit Mozilla Foundation and its wholly owned subsidiary, the for-profit Mozilla Corporation, which develops and publishes the Firefox web browser and the Gecko browser engine. Its stated mission is to keep the internet an open, accessible global public resource, and it runs trustworthy-AI programs including Mozilla.ai, Mozilla Ventures, Mozilla Builders, and the 0Din bug bounty. Its RFI response to the OSTP AI Action Plan was filed under the single 'Mozilla' banner covering both entities.
justification: Mozilla's primary operating activity is designing, developing, and distributing packaged software (the Firefox browser and Gecko engine) for general use, which is the defining activity of software publishing.

alternates.justification: Much of Mozilla's work is open-source software engineering, though it is published as a general-use product rather than custom client work.
The Mozilla Foundation side conducts internet-policy and trustworthy-AI advocacy, but this is secondary to product development.

alternates.naics_title: Computing Infrastructure Providers, Data Processing, Web Hosting, and Related Services
alternates.justification: Mozilla operates cloud-connected services such as sync and AI model deployment tooling, but hosting is not its primary line of activity.

category_justification: The submission states Mozilla's top entity is the non-profit Mozilla Foundation with the Mozilla Corporation as its wholly owned subsidiary, and it describes itself as an independent, mission-driven public-interest organization, though the NITRD respondent index labels it 'Private sector' because the revenue-generating browser work sits in the taxable subsidiary.

name: NJEdge
description: NJEdge, doing business as Edge, is a member-owned New Jersey nonprofit that operates a high-performance optical fiber research and education network serving colleges, universities, K-12 districts, government agencies, hospitals, and nonprofits across the Mid-Atlantic. It provides connectivity and network management (EdgeNet), cybersecurity and identity services (EdgeSecure), cloud and virtualization (EdgeCloud), educational technology, professional services, and a consortium purchasing program (EdgeMarket). It also connects its members to Internet2 and hosts communities of practice and professional development events.
justification: Edge's core activity is operating and providing access to a wired optical fiber network for member institutions, which is the defining activity of a wired telecommunications carrier.

alternates.naics_title: Computing Infrastructure Providers, Data Processing, Web Hosting, and Related Services
alternates.justification: Its EdgeCloud line delivers cloud, virtualization, and storage infrastructure to members.
Edge provides identity, security, and IT support services that fall outside pure network transport.
The consortium exists to support higher-education institutions with technology and procurement services.

category_justification: Edge self-describes as a member-owned nonprofit whose core business is delivering network, cloud, and procurement services to institutions rather than lobbying for members' collective interests, though its member-ownership and 'professional association' framing make a trade/coalition reading arguable.

name: NSF AI2ES
resolved_name: NSF AI Institute for Research on Trustworthy AI in Weather, Climate, and Coastal Oceanography (AI2ES), led by the University of Oklahoma
description: NSF AI2ES is one of the inaugural National Science Foundation National AI Research Institutes, headquartered at and led by the University of Oklahoma under principal investigator Amy McGovern. It conducts research across foundational AI, Earth system science, and risk communication to improve prediction of high-impact atmospheric, ocean, and coastal phenomena using trustworthy AI methods. It is a multi-institution collaboration with co-PIs at SUNY Albany, Colorado State University, North Carolina State University, and Texas A&M University-Corpus Christi, and it also develops AI curricula and workforce programs.
naics_title: Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology)
justification: The institute's primary activity is federally funded scientific research and development in atmospheric, ocean, and computer science, which fits physical and engineering sciences R&D.

alternates.justification: AI2ES is an organized research unit hosted by the University of Oklahoma and staffed by university faculty and students, with an explicit education and training mission.

alternates.naics_title: Research and Development in the Social Sciences and Humanities
alternates.justification: One of its three research thrusts is risk communication, a social science area, but it is a minority of the portfolio.
The institute produces and disseminates AI code repositories and tools, though as a research output rather than a service line.

category_justification: AI2ES is an NSF-funded research institute headquartered at the University of Oklahoma with co-PIs at four other universities, and the NITRD respondent index labels it 'Academia'.

name: NTI Bio
resolved_name: NTI | bio (Global Biological Policy and Programs), a program of the Nuclear Threat Initiative
description: NTI | bio is the global biological policy and programs division of the Nuclear Threat Initiative, a Washington, DC nonprofit security organization founded in 2001 by Ted Turner and Sam Nunn. It works to reduce catastrophic biological risks through policy development, the Global Health Security Index, the Global Biosecurity Innovation and Risk Reduction Initiative, and the International Biosecurity and Biosafety Initiative for Science (IBBIS). Its AI-related work focuses on the biosecurity implications of AI biodesign tools and foundation models.
justification: Its primary activity is nonprofit policy advocacy and norm-building aimed at reducing global biological and security threats rather than producing a commercial product or service.

alternates.naics_title: Research and Development in the Social Sciences and Humanities
alternates.justification: NTI | bio produces substantial policy research and analytical indices such as the Global Health Security Index.
It convenes international stakeholder communities on biosecurity, a civic convening function.
NTI funds and incubates external initiatives such as IBBIS, though grantmaking is not its main activity.

category_justification: NTI is a registered 501(c)(3) nonprofit with a public-interest global security mission and no membership base, and the NITRD respondent index labels it 'Non-profit'.

name: NYU
description: New York University is a large private research university founded in 1831 and headquartered in Greenwich Village, New York City. It grants bachelor's, master's, doctoral, and professional degrees across schools including Arts and Science, Tandon School of Engineering, Stern School of Business, and the School of Law. It also operates degree-granting portal campuses in Abu Dhabi and Shanghai and conducts extensive sponsored research, including AI and technology policy work.
justification: NYU's primary activity is offering academic instruction leading to baccalaureate and graduate degrees, the defining activity of this code.
category_justification: NYU is an accredited degree-granting private research university, and the NITRD respondent index labels it 'Academia'.

name: National Committee for Quality Assurance
description: The National Committee for Quality Assurance is an independent Washington, DC nonprofit founded in 1990 that accredits and certifies health care organizations, including health plans, provider practices, and credentialing organizations. It develops and maintains HEDIS, the Healthcare Effectiveness Data and Information Set, a widely used set of standardized health care quality measures used by employers, regulators, and public programs. It also runs recognition programs such as Patient-Centered Medical Home and publishes comparative quality ratings.
naics_title: All Other Professional, Scientific, and Technical Services
justification: NCQA's primary activity is providing professional accreditation, certification, and quality-measurement services to health care organizations, a technical service not captured by a more specific code.

alternates.justification: Standards-setting and accreditation bodies in a professional field are frequently classified here, though NCQA is not membership-based.

alternates.naics_title: Administrative Management and General Management Consulting Services
alternates.justification: Its accreditation surveys and quality-improvement guidance function much like organizational performance consulting.
NCQA advances a public-interest health care quality agenda and engages in health policy, but this is secondary to its accreditation operations.

category_justification: NCQA is an independent 501(c)(3) nonprofit delivering accreditation and quality-measurement services with no membership base representing collective interests, and the NITRD respondent index labels it 'Non-profit'.

name: National Congress of American Indians
description: The National Congress of American Indians, founded in 1944 and based in Washington, DC, is the oldest and largest national organization representing American Indian and Alaska Native tribal governments. Its membership consists of federally and state-recognized tribal nations along with individual Native people and organizations, and it advocates before Congress, federal agencies, and the courts on tribal sovereignty, treaty rights, and self-determination. It also conducts policy research through its Policy Research Center and convenes annual conventions where member tribes set resolutions.
justification: NCAI's primary activity is advocating for the rights and interests of tribal nations and Native people before government, which fits social advocacy organizations.

alternates.justification: Its core work is influencing federal legislation and policy on behalf of member tribes.
It functions as a membership convening body with annual conventions and a resolutions process.

alternates.naics_title: Research and Development in the Social Sciences and Humanities
alternates.justification: Its Policy Research Center produces original social science research on Native communities, but this supports rather than defines the organization.

category_justification: NCAI is explicitly membership-based, with tribal nations as its members, and its core activity is representing those members' collective interests before the federal government, which overrides the index's generic 'Non-profit' label.

name: National Payroll Reporting Consortium
description: The National Payroll Reporting Consortium is a nonprofit trade association whose members are payroll service providers that process payroll and employment tax filings for well over a million US employers. It works with federal and state tax, labor, and child support agencies to improve the efficiency and standardization of payroll-related reporting and electronic filing requirements. It regularly files comments with agencies such as the IRS, DOL, and state regulators on behalf of the payroll services industry.
justification: NPRC's primary activity is representing the collective regulatory and reporting interests of member payroll service companies before government, the defining activity of a business association.

alternates.justification: Its members are payroll and tax reporting specialists, giving it some characteristics of a professional body.
It engages in sustained public policy advocacy, though on behalf of an industry rather than a social cause.
Its subject matter is payroll processing and employment tax reporting, but the consortium itself does not perform those services.

category_justification: NPRC is a membership consortium of payroll service provider companies formed to represent their collective interests with government, and the NITRD index labels it 'Industry/professional/scientific association'.

name: Natural Intelligence Systems
description: Natural Intelligence Systems is a privately held, venture-backed technology company based in Boise, Idaho, that develops pattern-based artificial intelligence and neuromorphic computing technology. Its products include the Natural Intelligence Machine Learning system (NIML), which encodes data into patterns and produces explainable classifications, and a neuromorphic computing platform for model development, training, and prediction. The company is also designing the Natural Neural Processor (NNP), a semiconductor device intended to accelerate AI and analytics workloads. It is an independent company, not a subsidiary, and the NITRD respondent index lists it as private sector.
justification: The company's central product line is the Natural Neural Processor, a purpose-designed neuromorphic semiconductor device, placing its primary activity in fabless semiconductor design and development.

alternates.justification: Its currently shipping offerings are software machine-learning and neuromorphic computing systems licensed to customers.

alternates.naics_title: Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology)
alternates.justification: As a small pre-commercial startup, much of its activity is engineering R&D on novel AI architectures.
It markets a neuromorphic computing system, which could be read as computing hardware manufacturing.

category_justification: Crunchbase and the NITRD index identify it as a private venture-backed for-profit startup with named founders and Techstars investment.

name: New America
description: New America is a nonpartisan, nonprofit think tank and civic enterprise headquartered in Washington, DC, founded in 1999. It conducts policy research, publishes analysis, and runs programs across technology, education, national security, and economic policy, including its Open Technology Institute, which focuses on internet, broadband, and AI governance. It is an independent 501(c)(3) organization funded by foundations, corporations, and individual donors rather than a unit of a larger parent.
naics_title: Research and Development in the Social Sciences and Humanities
justification: Its primary activity is producing original public-policy research and analysis in the social sciences, the standard classification for a think tank.

alternates.justification: Several New America programs, notably the Open Technology Institute, advocate for specific policy outcomes.
It describes itself as a civic enterprise convening public debate and fellowship communities.

alternates.naics_title: All Other Professional, Scientific, and Technical Services
alternates.justification: A residual professional-services code for its mixed research, convening, and technical assistance work.

category_justification: It is a 501(c)(3) mission-driven research institution with no membership base, no degree-granting function, and no government affiliation; the NITRD index labels it Non-profit.

name: New York State
resolved_name: New York State Executive Chamber (Office of the Governor of New York)
description: The submission recorded as "New York State" was filed by the New York State Executive Chamber, the office of Governor Kathy Hochul, and signed by Kathryn Garcia, Director of State Operations and Infrastructure. The Executive Chamber is the chief executive office of New York State government, directing state agencies and setting statewide policy, including on technology and artificial intelligence. It is a unit of the government of the State of New York, not a private organization.
justification: The Executive Chamber is the office of a state chief executive, whose primary activity is executive direction of state government, matching Executive Offices exactly.
category_justification: The comment was signed by New York's Director of State Operations on behalf of the Governor's Executive Chamber, a state-level government body; the NITRD index labels it Non-federal government.

name: NewDEAL Forum
resolved_name: NewDEAL Forum (policy arm of the NewDEAL network of elected officials)
description: The NewDEAL Forum is a Washington, DC-based 501(c)(3) organization that identifies, develops, and elevates innovative state and local policy ideas described as pro-growth progressive. It is the policy-focused sister organization of the NewDEAL, a national network of rising state and local elected officials, and shares leadership with it under CEO Debbie Cox Bultan. Its work is carried out largely through issue task forces staffed by NewDEAL member officials, an annual Ideas Summit, and published policy playbooks on topics including artificial intelligence.
justification: Its primary activity is promoting a defined set of policy positions and spreading them among public officials, which fits social advocacy rather than academic research production.

alternates.justification: It functions as the convening arm of a civic network of elected officials, running summits and peer task forces.

alternates.naics_title: Research and Development in the Social Sciences and Humanities
alternates.justification: It publishes original policy research reports and playbooks in the manner of a think tank.
Its constituency is a defined professional class, elected officeholders, organized into an affiliated network.

category_justification: It is the policy arm of the NewDEAL, explicitly a coalition-style network of member elected officials whose task forces produce its work, so the membership-base rule overrides the index's Non-profit label.

name: Nielsen
description: Nielsen is a global for-profit audience measurement, data, and analytics company that measures what audiences watch and listen to across television, streaming, audio, and digital media. Its comment describes the firm as both a developer and deployer of AI models and a leader in independent audience measurement, and it was signed by Executive Chairman David W. Kenny. Nielsen's business units include Gracenote, a media and entertainment metadata provider it operates as a subsidiary brand.
naics_title: Marketing Research and Public Opinion Polling
justification: Nielsen's primary activity is independent measurement of media audiences and consumer behavior sold to media and advertising clients, the core of marketing research services.

alternates.naics_title: Computing Infrastructure Providers, Data Processing, Web Hosting, and Related Services
alternates.justification: Its measurement business rests on large-scale data processing and analytics delivery platforms.

alternates.naics_title: Web Search Portals and All Other Information Services
alternates.justification: The Gracenote unit licenses entertainment metadata databases, an information-services activity.
Nielsen delivers measurement products through licensed analytics software platforms.

category_justification: Nielsen is a publicly recognized for-profit commercial measurement firm and the NITRD index lists it as private sector.

name: Noema Research
description: Noema Research is a small AI safety and security research organization whose stated aim is securing access to generative AI capabilities by treating advanced model capabilities as a controlled resource governed with established information-security methods. Its work spans technical research on identity and access management for AI systems, red-teaming and stress-testing of frontier models, and developer tooling such as Pinboard, a command-line tool for working with generative systems. Its site names Open Philanthropy and Microsoft as supporters, and the NITRD respondent index classifies it as a non-profit; it does not appear to be a subsidiary of a larger organization.
naics_title: Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology)
justification: Its primary activity is technical research and engineering on AI security, access control, and model evaluation, which falls under physical and engineering sciences R&D.

alternates.naics_title: Research and Development in the Social Sciences and Humanities
alternates.justification: Much of its output addresses AI governance and policy questions rather than laboratory science.

alternates.naics_title: Other Scientific and Technical Consulting Services
alternates.justification: Its red-teaming and capability-assessment work resembles technical security consulting.
It publishes and distributes developer tools such as Pinboard.

category_justification: The NITRD respondent index labels it Non-profit and it is philanthropically funded by Open Philanthropy, though its website does not state a legal form.

name: OCHIN
resolved_name: OCHIN, Inc. (originally Oregon Community Health Information Network)
description: OCHIN is a Portland, Oregon-based nonprofit health information technology and consultancy organization serving community health centers and rural providers nationwide. It implements, hosts, and supports a shared Epic electronic health record platform for roughly 300 member care organizations and adds workforce training, revenue cycle, security, and operational support services. It also maintains a practice-based research network that uses its pooled clinical data for health services research; it is an independent nonprofit, not a subsidiary.
justification: Its primary activity is designing, implementing, integrating, and supporting electronic health record systems for client health care organizations.

alternates.naics_title: Computing Infrastructure Providers, Data Processing, Web Hosting, and Related Services
alternates.justification: OCHIN hosts a shared Epic instance and processes clinical data on behalf of its member clinics.
It performs substantial custom configuration and development work on the shared EHR platform.
It describes itself as a nonprofit consultancy offering operational, financial, and workforce advisory services.

category_justification: It is a mission-driven 501(c)(3) health IT organization serving safety-net providers, labeled Non-profit in the NITRD index, and is not a university, government unit, or membership advocacy body.

name: OHSU
description: Oregon Health & Science University is Oregon's only public academic health center, based in Portland, and operates as an independent public corporation of the state. It grants degrees through schools of medicine, nursing, dentistry, public health, and pharmacy, and conducts extensive biomedical and health services research. It also runs a large hospital and clinic system, including OHSU Hospital and Doernbecher Children's Hospital; the NITRD respondent index classifies its submission as Academia.
justification: OHSU is a degree-granting academic health university whose primary institutional activity is professional and graduate health sciences education and associated research.

alternates.justification: A large share of OHSU's revenue and workforce is in its academic hospital and clinical operations.

alternates.naics_title: Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology)
alternates.justification: OHSU is a major recipient of federal biomedical research funding and runs substantial research institutes.

alternates.naics_title: Offices of Physicians (except Mental Health Specialists)
alternates.justification: It operates an extensive faculty practice and outpatient clinic network.

category_justification: OHSU is a degree-granting public academic health university and the NITRD index labels the submission Academia.

name: OpenAI
description: OpenAI is a San Francisco-based artificial intelligence research and deployment company known for the GPT family of large language models, ChatGPT, DALL-E, and its developer API. It operates as a capped-profit company (OpenAI Global, LLC) governed by the nonprofit OpenAI Inc., and earns revenue primarily from consumer and enterprise subscriptions and paid API access to its models. It submitted a response to the NITRD AI Action Plan RFI as a private sector respondent.
justification: OpenAI's primary revenue-generating activity is developing and licensing proprietary AI software products (ChatGPT, API models) to consumers, developers, and enterprises, which is the design-develop-publish pattern of software publishing.

alternates.naics_title: Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology)
alternates.justification: OpenAI self-describes as an AI research company and runs large-scale frontier model research programs.

alternates.naics_title: Computing Infrastructure Providers, Data Processing, Web Hosting, and Related Services
alternates.justification: Its API delivers model inference as a hosted, metered computing service rather than as installed software.
Some enterprise engagements involve bespoke deployment and integration work, though this is not the core business.

category_justification: OpenAI is a for-profit commercial AI company selling subscriptions and API access, and the RFI respondent index labels it 'Private sector'.

name: PRECURSOR SPC
description: Precursor SPC is a geospatial event intelligence company that operates a network of proprietary multi-sensor ground stations and satellite systems to forecast earthquakes and space weather events. It applies machine learning to earth-observation and ionospheric data to produce deterministic forecasts of event location, magnitude, and timing, and has delivered tools to U.S. and U.K. agencies. It is organized as a social purpose corporation and has raised capital through an online public offering; its RFI submission concerned operational earthquake forecasting.
naics_title: Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology)
justification: Its core activity is applied geophysical and space-physics research to develop novel earthquake and space-weather forecasting capability from proprietary sensor data.

alternates.naics_title: All Other Professional, Scientific, and Technical Services
alternates.justification: Selling forecasts as a service most closely parallels weather forecasting services, which fall in this residual professional-services code.
The company collects and interprets geophysical ground-station data and describes itself as geospatial intelligence.

alternates.naics_title: Computing Infrastructure Providers, Data Processing, Web Hosting, and Related Services
alternates.justification: Its output is delivered as processed data feeds and machine-learning products from collected sensor streams.

category_justification: It is a for-profit social purpose corporation selling forecasting products and raising investor capital, and the RFI index lists it as 'Private sector'.

name: PWC
description: PwC (PricewaterhouseCoopers) is one of the Big Four global professional services networks, providing assurance and audit, tax, and management and technology consulting services. Its U.S. member firm serves corporate and public sector clients across industries and maintains a large technology and AI advisory practice. It filed a response to the NITRD AI Action Plan RFI as a private sector respondent.
justification: PwC's foundational and licensed primary line of business is public accounting, audit, and assurance performed by CPA-licensed member firms, with tax and consulting built around that practice.

alternates.naics_title: Administrative Management and General Management Consulting Services
alternates.justification: PwC's advisory arm is a very large management consulting practice and may be the unit that authored the AI policy comment.
Much of its work is specialized consulting outside general management, including technology and regulatory advisory.
PwC delivers substantial systems integration and AI implementation engagements for clients.

category_justification: PwC is a for-profit professional services partnership commenting in its own capacity, though as an advisory firm its positions also reflect work done for unnamed corporate clients.

name: Pair Team
description: Pair Team is a California-based, technology-enabled care company that operates as a community care hub connecting high-needs Medicaid members to primary care, behavioral health, and social services. It contracts with health plans and partners with clinics and community-based organizations to deliver enhanced care management and care coordination, and converted to a public benefit corporation in 2025. Its RFI response was submitted under the name of its chief medical officer, Nate Favini, and it is listed as a private sector respondent.
naics_title: All Other Miscellaneous Ambulatory Health Care Services
justification: Its primary activity is delivering non-facility-based care coordination and enhanced care management services to Medicaid patients, a miscellaneous ambulatory health care service rather than software sales.

alternates.justification: Pair Team delivers clinical and behavioral outpatient care to enrolled members through its virtual and community care model.

alternates.naics_title: Offices of All Other Miscellaneous Health Practitioners
alternates.justification: Care is provided by multidisciplinary teams of practitioners and community health workers.
The company builds and licenses its own care-coordination platform used by partner clinics.

category_justification: It is a venture-backed for-profit public benefit corporation contracting with Medicaid health plans, and the RFI index labels it 'Private sector'.

name: Palo Alto Networks
description: Palo Alto Networks is a publicly traded American cybersecurity company headquartered in Santa Clara, California. It sells network security platforms including next-generation firewalls, cloud-native application protection, and AI-driven security operations products, increasingly delivered as software and subscription services. It submitted a private sector response to the NITRD AI Action Plan RFI.
justification: The large majority of its revenue now comes from security software subscriptions and support licensed to enterprises, with hardware appliances a declining share.

alternates.justification: It designs and integrates enterprise security architectures and provides managed detection and incident response services.

alternates.naics_title: Computing Infrastructure Providers, Data Processing, Web Hosting, and Related Services
alternates.justification: Its cloud-delivered security services process customer traffic and telemetry on company-operated infrastructure.

alternates.naics_title: Computer Terminal and Other Computer Peripheral Equipment Manufacturing
alternates.justification: It still designs and sells physical firewall appliances as part of its product line.

category_justification: It is a publicly traded for-profit corporation (NASDAQ: PANW) and the RFI index lists it as 'Private sector'.

name: Partnership for AI Infrastructure
description: The Partnership for AI Infrastructure is a U.S. coalition of technology companies advocating for federal support and funding of advanced computing and AI infrastructure. Its members include AMD, Arm, Hewlett Packard Enterprise, and Intel, and its stated priorities are scientific computing, critical infrastructure security, and national security applications of AI. It engages in policy advocacy on behalf of its corporate members rather than delivering services to the public.
justification: Its sole activity is collective policy advocacy and public-affairs representation on behalf of dues-paying member companies, which is the defining activity of a business association.

alternates.justification: Its public-facing output is issue advocacy campaigns aimed at federal policymakers.
It convenes technical industry leaders around a shared computing agenda.
Coalitions of this kind are sometimes staffed and run by government-relations consultancies.

category_justification: Its website describes it as a coalition whose members are named technology companies (AMD, Arm, HPE, Intel) organized to advance their shared policy interests, so the membership-base rule overrides the index's 'Non-profit' label.

name: Pathway For Patient Health
description: Pathway for Patient Health is a consortium of chief quality officers and quality leaders from life sciences companies focused on improving product quality, safety, and patient outcomes. It convenes conferences, forums, and working groups, sponsors quality and innovation initiatives, and builds industry-university workforce partnerships. In 2024 it launched a separate nonprofit arm, Quality Champions for Life, to house its educational and student-mentoring programs.
justification: Its primary activity is convening and serving a membership of life sciences quality professionals through conferences, working groups, and professional development, the defining activity of a professional organization.

alternates.justification: Members join as representatives of their life sciences employers, giving the consortium an industry-association character.
A substantial share of its programming is professional education and upskilling for industry employees.
Its stated mission of improving patient safety globally has a public-interest advocacy dimension.

category_justification: It self-describes as a consortium of chief quality officers drawn from member life sciences companies, so despite the index's 'Non-profit' label the membership-base rule applies.

name: PauseAI NYC
resolved_name: PauseAI NYC (New York City local group of PauseAI US)
description: PauseAI NYC is the New York City local group of PauseAI US, a volunteer-driven AI safety advocacy organization that campaigns for a pause on frontier AI development and for binding international regulation. The chapter organizes protests, letter-writing and lobbying actions, and public meetups aimed at policymakers and the public. It is part of the broader international PauseAI movement founded in 2023 and is not a commercial or membership-interest body.
justification: Its entire activity is volunteer-organized public advocacy and protest aimed at changing AI policy, which is squarely social advocacy.

alternates.justification: As a local chapter it functions substantially as a civic meetup group for volunteers.
Its lobbying and legislator-contact campaigns target elected officials directly.
The parent PauseAI network is philanthropically funded, though the chapter itself makes no grants.

category_justification: It is an unincorporated volunteer chapter of the nonprofit PauseAI US pursuing a public-interest AI safety mission rather than representing members' own collective interests, and the RFI index labels it 'Non-profit'.

name: PauseAI US
description: PauseAI US is a San Francisco-headquartered grassroots advocacy organization, incorporated as a 501(c)(3) nonprofit in 2024, that campaigns for an international pause on the development of frontier artificial intelligence systems. It organizes local volunteer chapters in cities such as San Francisco, New York, Chicago, Portland, Phoenix and Washington DC, which lobby lawmakers, stage public protests and conduct media outreach about catastrophic AI risk. It is the separately incorporated US affiliate within the broader PauseAI movement, which has parallel national entities in the Netherlands, France, the United Kingdom and other countries.
justification: The organization's primary activity is public-issue advocacy and grassroots campaigning to influence AI policy, which is exactly the activity described by Other Social Advocacy Organizations.
category_justification: Its own about page states it is an incorporated 501(c)(3) public-interest NGO advancing a cause rather than a body representing the collective interests of dues-paying members, though its chapter structure makes the nonprofit/coalition line arguable.

name: PepsiCo
description: PepsiCo, Inc. is a publicly traded American multinational food, snack and beverage corporation headquartered in Purchase, New York. It manufactures, markets and distributes carbonated and non-carbonated drinks under brands such as Pepsi, Mountain Dew and Gatorade, and salty and convenient foods through its Frito-Lay and Quaker Foods businesses. Its operations span company-owned bottling, concentrate production, contract manufacturing and direct-store-delivery distribution across North America and international markets.
justification: PepsiCo's beverage manufacturing and concentrate operations are its flagship and largest single line of business, and the company is conventionally classified to soft drink manufacturing, though its snack food segment is nearly as large.

alternates.justification: The Frito-Lay salty snack business is comparable in revenue to the beverage business and would place the company in snack food manufacturing.
A diversified food conglomerate spanning many prepared-food lines could be coded to the residual food manufacturing category.
PepsiCo produces ready-to-drink coffee and tea products through partnerships, but this is a small share of output.

category_justification: PepsiCo is a NASDAQ-listed for-profit corporation, and the NITRD respondent index labels the submitter as private sector.

name: Proof.com
resolved_name: Proof (Notarize, Inc., doing business as Proof.com)
description: Proof, legally Notarize, Inc. and operating as Proof.com, is a for-profit software company that runs an identity-centric platform for authenticating parties to high-value digital transactions. Its cloud products include Identify, Verify, Sign, Notarize, Certify, Close and Defend, covering remote online notarization, electronic signature, document certification and real-time fraud detection, plus a Digital ID wallet. Customers are concentrated in real estate, financial services, credit unions, insurance, automotive and retirement services, and the company has published an x401 standard for authenticating AI agents in transactions.
justification: Proof's primary activity is developing and licensing a proprietary cloud software platform for identity verification and electronic transaction execution, which fits software publishing.

alternates.justification: The company's flagship Notarize product delivers remote online notarial acts through a network of commissioned notaries, the defining activity of this code.

alternates.naics_title: Investigation and Personal Background Check Services
alternates.justification: Identity proofing, credential analysis and fraud screening are the substance of much of what Proof sells to enterprise clients.
The offering could be read as a managed computer-related transaction service rather than a packaged software product.

category_justification: Proof is a venture-backed for-profit technology vendor selling subscription products, and the NITRD respondent index labels it private sector.

name: Protect AI
resolved_name: Protect AI, Inc. (acquired by Palo Alto Networks in 2025)
description: Protect AI was a Seattle-based cybersecurity company founded in 2022 that specialized in securing artificial intelligence and machine learning systems and supply chains. Its products included Guardian for model scanning, Recon for automated red teaming of large language models, Layer for runtime AI security, the open-source ModelScan and NB Defense tools, and the huntr AI bug bounty community. It filed this RFI response as an independent company; Palo Alto Networks announced its intent to acquire Protect AI in April 2025 and completed the acquisition later that year, folding the technology into its Prisma AIRS platform.
justification: Protect AI's primary activity was developing and licensing proprietary security software products for AI and ML pipelines, which is software publishing.

alternates.justification: Security vendors that deploy and integrate protective tooling into customer environments are frequently classified as computer systems design firms.
Managed model scanning and red-teaming delivered as an ongoing service could fall under other computer related services.

alternates.naics_title: Computing Infrastructure Providers, Data Processing, Web Hosting, and Related Services
alternates.justification: The products are delivered from a hosted cloud platform that processes customer model and telemetry data.

category_justification: Protect AI was a venture-funded for-profit corporation later acquired by a public company, and the NITRD respondent index labels it private sector.

name: Quantum Connect AI
description: Quantum Connect AI is a small for-profit technology vendor that sells AI-powered voice and communication automation to automotive dealerships. Its platform provides autonomous voice agents that answer unanswered inbound dealership calls and agentic business development center agents that run compliance-gated outbound calling campaigns. The system writes activity back in real time to major automotive customer relationship management platforms including VinSolutions, DealerSocket and Elead.
justification: The company's primary activity is developing and licensing a proprietary AI voice-agent and CRM-integration software product to dealership customers.

alternates.naics_title: Telemarketing Bureaus and Other Contact Centers
alternates.justification: The service functions as an outsourced inbound and outbound calling operation for dealerships, differing from a human contact center mainly in that the agents are automated.
A small vendor that configures and integrates voice agents into each dealership's CRM may be primarily performing custom programming work.

alternates.naics_title: Computing Infrastructure Providers, Data Processing, Web Hosting, and Related Services
alternates.justification: The offering is a hosted service that processes call and customer data on the vendor's infrastructure.

category_justification: Its website and LinkedIn page present it as a commercial dealership technology vendor, and the NITRD respondent index labels it private sector.

name: RAD Security
resolved_name: RAD Security (formerly KSOC, Kubernetes Security Operations Center)
description: RAD Security is a venture-backed cloud-native cybersecurity company, formerly named KSOC, that was renamed in 2024 to reflect a broadened scope beyond Kubernetes posture management. Its platform builds behavioral fingerprints of workload and identity activity to detect and respond to threats in Kubernetes clusters, containers and cloud environments in real time. The company is led by co-founder and chief executive Brooke Motta, who submitted the firm's response to this RFI.
justification: RAD Security's primary activity is developing and licensing a proprietary cloud-native detection and response software platform, which is software publishing.

alternates.justification: Security platforms that are deployed into and integrated with customer cloud infrastructure are often coded as computer systems design services.

alternates.naics_title: Computing Infrastructure Providers, Data Processing, Web Hosting, and Related Services
alternates.justification: The platform is delivered as a hosted service that ingests and processes large volumes of customer runtime telemetry.
Continuous managed threat detection and response could be treated as an ongoing computer-related service rather than a licensed product.

category_justification: RAD Security is a privately held venture-funded for-profit vendor and the NITRD respondent index labels the submission private sector.

name: RERC
resolved_name: Rehabilitation Engineering Research Centers (joint submission by six NIDILRR-funded RERCs, led by the RERC on ICT and Accessibility (CREATE))
description: RERC here refers to a joint filing by six Rehabilitation Engineering Research Centers, federally funded research programs supported by the National Institute on Disability, Independent Living, and Rehabilitation Research and hosted at universities and nonprofit research institutes. The signatories are the RERC on ICT and Accessibility (CREATE), the RERC on Augmentative and Alternative Communication, the RERC on Blindness and Low Vision, the RERC on Deaf and Hard of Hearing Technology, the TRACE RERC at the University of Maryland with Raising the Floor, and the TechSAge RERC on technologies to support aging with long-term disabilities. Their comment argues that accessibility and disability perspectives must be built into the national AI Action Plan, covering open-source model development, accessible interfaces, data augmentation, privacy of disability-related data, and disability-specific AI bias.
naics_title: Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology)
justification: The primary activity of Rehabilitation Engineering Research Centers is applied engineering and assistive-technology research and development, which falls under physical and engineering sciences R&D.

alternates.naics_title: Research and Development in the Social Sciences and Humanities
alternates.justification: Much RERC work is human-computer interaction and disability studies research on how people with disabilities use technology, which is social science research.
Most of the signing centers are administrative units housed inside degree-granting universities such as Washington, Penn State, Maryland and Gallaudet.
The submission itself is a collective disability-accessibility advocacy statement directed at federal policy.

category_justification: The filing is a collective statement by mission-driven, federally funded public-interest research centers rather than by any single university, government agency, or dues-paying membership body, though several individual centers are university sub-units.

name: Ronawk
description: Ronawk, Inc. is a privately held biotechnology company based in the Kansas City metropolitan area, in Overland Park and Olathe, Kansas. It designs and manufactures 3D-printed hydrogel cell culture products, principally its T-Block and B-Block bio-blocks, which allow stem cells and other cells to be expanded and maintained at lower cost and higher density than conventional flask-based culture. The company sells these consumables to research, biomanufacturing and regenerative medicine customers, has partnered with B9Creations on 3D bioprinting scale-up, and has flown its blocks on a space mission experiment.
justification: Ronawk's primary activity is manufacturing biological cell-culture matrix products used to grow and expand living cells, which fits non-diagnostic biological product manufacturing.

alternates.naics_title: Research and Development in Biotechnology (except Nanobiotechnology)
alternates.justification: As an early-stage biotech startup, a large share of its activity is biotechnology research and development on cell expansion and tissue engineering.
Hydrogel scaffolds aimed at regenerative medicine and tissue applications could be classified as medical supplies manufacturing.
The blocks are laboratory consumables sold alongside culture workflows, adjacent to laboratory apparatus manufacturing.

category_justification: Ronawk is a for-profit venture-backed biotech startup profiled in CB Insights and regional business press, and the NITRD respondent index labels it private sector.

name: Roots Automation
description: Roots Automation is a New York-based private technology company that develops AI-powered 'Digital Coworkers' and an autonomous workforce platform for the insurance industry. Its products, including the InsurGPT domain-specific generative AI model, automate document intake, claims processing, and underwriting support tasks for carriers, brokers, and third-party administrators. The company sells its software on a subscription basis to commercial insurance clients and was listed in the NITRD AI Action Plan RFI index as a private-sector respondent.
justification: Its primary activity is developing and licensing proprietary AI/automation software products (Digital Coworkers, InsurGPT) to insurance customers, which is software publishing.

alternates.justification: Deployments are configured per client, which can resemble custom programming services.
The platform integrates with insurers' existing claims and policy systems.
The offering is framed as outsourced back-office document processing labor.

category_justification: It is a venture-backed for-profit software vendor and the official RFI respondent index labels it 'Private sector'.

name: SCORE-NYC
resolved_name: SCORE New York City (chapter of SCORE Association)
description: SCORE-NYC is the New York City chapter of the SCORE Association, a national nonprofit and resource partner of the U.S. Small Business Administration. It uses volunteer business executives to provide free one-on-one mentoring, workshops, and educational resources to small business owners and prospective entrepreneurs in the five boroughs. The RFI submission was filed under the name of an individual chapter volunteer, and the official respondent index labels the submitter 'Non-profit'.
justification: The chapter's primary activity is delivering business mentoring, seminars, and management training to small business owners rather than selling consulting engagements.

alternates.naics_title: Administrative Management and General Management Consulting Services
alternates.justification: One-on-one mentoring on business strategy and operations closely resembles general management consulting.
It is a volunteer-staffed civic chapter organized to serve a local community.
The chapter provides supplementary educational support and counseling rather than formal instruction.

category_justification: SCORE is a 501(c)(3) mission-driven volunteer mentoring organization and SBA resource partner that serves the public rather than dues-paying members, and the RFI index labels it 'Non-profit'.

name: Salesforce
description: Salesforce, Inc. is a publicly traded American enterprise software company headquartered in San Francisco. It publishes cloud-based customer relationship management applications spanning sales, service, marketing, commerce, and analytics, along with the Agentforce and Einstein AI platforms and the Slack collaboration product. It sells these products worldwide on a software-as-a-service subscription model and filed its RFI response as a private-sector commenter.
justification: Salesforce's overwhelming primary activity is developing, publishing, and licensing its own packaged cloud application software.
category_justification: It is a publicly traded for-profit corporation (NYSE: CRM) listed as 'Private sector' in the official respondent index.

name: Sam Brinton The Trevor Project
resolved_name: The Trevor Project (submission associated with Sam Brinton, former Vice President of Advocacy and Government Affairs)
description: The Trevor Project is a U.S. nonprofit organization that provides 24/7 crisis intervention and suicide prevention services to lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender, queer, and questioning young people, alongside research and public policy advocacy. Sam Brinton is a nuclear waste policy specialist who previously served as the organization's Vice President of Advocacy and Government Affairs, a role in which they represented the organization before federal policymakers. The record pairs a named individual with that organizational affiliation, so it is treated as a submission made on behalf of The Trevor Project.
justification: The organization's primary activity is operating crisis intervention and counseling helplines for at-risk youth, which falls under other individual and family social services.

alternates.justification: Its services are targeted specifically at LGBTQ young people under 25.
A substantial share of its work is public policy advocacy on LGBTQ youth issues.

alternates.naics_title: Offices of Mental Health Practitioners (except Physicians)
alternates.justification: Its counselors deliver mental health crisis support, though not as a clinical practice.

category_justification: The Trevor Project is a 501(c)(3) service-delivery and research organization with no membership base; the individual is named as an affiliated representative rather than as a private commenter.

name: SambaNova Systems
description: SambaNova Systems is a private Palo Alto-based company that designs Reconfigurable Dataflow Unit AI accelerator chips and the integrated DataScale systems built around them. It pairs this hardware with a software stack and the SambaNova Cloud inference service, selling full-stack AI platforms to enterprises, national laboratories, and government customers. The company is listed as a private-sector respondent in the NITRD AI Action Plan RFI index.
justification: Its core product and principal source of differentiation is the fabless design of RDU AI accelerator semiconductors sold in integrated systems.

alternates.naics_title: Computing Infrastructure Providers, Data Processing, Web Hosting, and Related Services
alternates.justification: SambaNova Cloud delivers hosted model inference capacity as a service.
The company also develops and licenses its SambaFlow compiler and model software stack.
DataScale racks are assembled electronic systems built from the company's boards.

category_justification: It is a venture-funded for-profit hardware and AI systems vendor labeled 'Private sector' in the official respondent index.

name: SandboxAQ
description: SandboxAQ is a private company spun out of Alphabet in 2022 that develops enterprise software combining artificial intelligence with quantum-derived methods, a combination it markets as 'AQ'. Its products include large quantitative models for drug discovery and materials science, AI-based navigation systems, and cryptographic management tools for post-quantum migration. It sells these to pharmaceutical, financial services, telecommunications, and government customers and responded to the RFI as a private-sector entity.
justification: Its commercial output is proprietary enterprise software products (AQtive Guard, large quantitative models) licensed to customers rather than contract research or hardware.

alternates.naics_title: Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology)
alternates.justification: Much of the company's activity is scientific R&D in quantum sensing, chemistry simulation, and cryptography.
Enterprise deployments involve substantial customer-specific engineering work.

alternates.naics_title: Other Scientific and Technical Consulting Services
alternates.justification: It advises clients on post-quantum cryptographic migration strategy.

category_justification: It is a for-profit venture-backed corporation and Alphabet spinout, listed as 'Private sector' in the RFI respondent index.

name: Save Our Standards
description: Save Our Standards is a Washington-based advocacy coalition of technology, automotive, retail, and public-interest organizations focused on standard-essential patent licensing policy. Its members, which include large technology firms, automotive suppliers, and trade associations such as CCIA and SIIA, advocate for enforcement of fair, reasonable, and non-discriminatory (FRAND) licensing commitments and against what they characterize as abusive SEP licensing practices. It educates policymakers and files comments in federal proceedings on behalf of its member organizations.
justification: Its primary activity is representing the collective policy interests of member companies and business associations before government, which is the business association activity.

alternates.justification: The coalition's public-facing work is issue advocacy on patent licensing policy.
Some participants are professional and scientific associations rather than firms.

alternates.naics_title: All Other Professional, Scientific, and Technical Services
alternates.justification: Its output could be read as specialized policy and technical advocacy services.

category_justification: It self-describes as a coalition of more than fifty member organizations advancing their shared SEP licensing interests, and the RFI index labels it an 'Industry/professional/scientific association'.

name: Schneider Electric
description: Schneider Electric SE is a publicly traded French multinational headquartered in Rueil-Malmaison that specializes in energy management and industrial automation. It manufactures and sells electrical distribution equipment, switchgear, circuit protection, uninterruptible power supplies, building management systems, and industrial control products, together with the EcoStruxure software and services layer. Its data center and grid infrastructure business is the basis of its interest in the U.S. AI Action Plan RFI, to which it responded as a private-sector commenter.
justification: Its largest primary activity is manufacturing low- and medium-voltage electrical distribution and switchgear apparatus for buildings, industry, and data centers.

alternates.justification: Its industrial automation segment produces relays, PLCs, drives, and process control equipment.

alternates.naics_title: All Other Miscellaneous Electrical Equipment and Component Manufacturing
alternates.justification: The company's UPS and other power products span a broad range of electrical equipment.
EcoStruxure and its acquired AVEVA business publish industrial software.

category_justification: It is a for-profit publicly listed corporation (Euronext: SU) and the official respondent index treats it as a company submission.

name: Scott County, Minnesota
resolved_name: Scott County, Minnesota (county government, State of Minnesota)
description: Scott County is a county government in the southwest Twin Cities metropolitan area of Minnesota, with its seat in Shakopee. It is governed by an elected five-member Board of Commissioners and delivers county-level services including property records and assessment, health and human services, public works and transit, sheriff and court support, and community development. The county submitted a response to the federal AI Action Plan RFI and is listed in the NITRD respondent index as a non-federal government submitter.
justification: A county governed by an elected board that combines executive and legislative functions over general-purpose local government is classified under combined executive and legislative offices.

alternates.justification: County central administrative and support services (records, assessment, finance, IT) fit general government support.
If the county board is treated primarily as a chief executive office rather than a combined body.

alternates.naics_title: Administration of Human Resource Programs (except Education, Public Health, and Veterans' Affairs Programs)
alternates.justification: Health and human services delivery is one of the county's largest program areas, though not its sole primary activity.

category_justification: Scott County is a general-purpose local (county) government unit in Minnesota, and the NITRD respondent index labels it 'Non-federal government'.

name: SecureBio
description: SecureBio is an independent US nonprofit research organization working to prevent catastrophic pandemics, founded by MIT Media Lab researcher Kevin Esvelt and closely associated with his Sculpting Evolution group. Its work spans nucleic acid synthesis screening (the SecureDNA project), early pandemic detection and environmental biosurveillance, and assessment of biosecurity risks created by AI and biotechnology tools. It is registered as a 501(c)(3) organization and is funded largely by philanthropic grants; the NITRD respondent index lists it as a non-profit submitter.
naics_title: Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology)
justification: SecureBio's primary activity is conducting applied life-sciences and biosecurity research and developing technical countermeasures, which is R&D in the physical, engineering, and life sciences.

alternates.naics_title: Research and Development in Biotechnology (except Nanobiotechnology)
alternates.justification: Its DNA-synthesis screening and pathogen-detection work is biotechnology R&D in the narrower sense.
A substantial share of its output is biosecurity policy advocacy and recommendations to government.

alternates.naics_title: Other Scientific and Technical Consulting Services
alternates.justification: It provides technical biosecurity advice to synthesis providers and policymakers.

category_justification: It is a registered 501(c)(3) research organization pursuing a public-interest pandemic-prevention mission with no membership base, and the NITRD index labels it 'Non-profit'.

name: ServiceNow
description: ServiceNow, Inc. is a publicly traded American enterprise software company headquartered in Santa Clara, California. It publishes the Now Platform, a cloud-based software-as-a-service suite for IT service management, IT operations, employee and customer workflows, and increasingly AI-driven workflow automation. The company filed its own response to the AI Action Plan RFI and is listed in the NITRD respondent index as a private-sector submitter.
justification: ServiceNow's primary activity is designing, publishing, and licensing its own enterprise workflow software platform, the defining activity of software publishers.

alternates.naics_title: Computing Infrastructure Providers, Data Processing, Web Hosting, and Related Services
alternates.justification: Its products are delivered as hosted multi-tenant cloud services running on its own infrastructure.
It also earns revenue from implementation, configuration, and professional services around the platform.
Customer-specific application development on the Now Platform is a secondary line of work.

category_justification: ServiceNow is a for-profit, NYSE-listed corporation commenting in its own commercial capacity.

name: Siemens USA
resolved_name: Siemens USA (US country organization of Siemens AG)
description: Siemens USA is the United States country organization of the German technology conglomerate Siemens AG, encompassing its US operating businesses and holding entity Siemens Corporation. Its US activities center on industrial automation and process control, industrial and engineering software, smart building and electrical infrastructure equipment, and rail mobility systems, with manufacturing, R&D, and software sites across the country. It filed the RFI response on behalf of Siemens' US operations and is listed in the NITRD respondent index as a private-sector submitter.
naics_title: Instruments and Related Products Manufacturing for Measuring, Displaying, and Controlling Industrial Process Variables
justification: Siemens' largest US business line is industrial automation and process control equipment, whose manufacture falls under industrial process control instruments; the conglomerate's breadth makes any single code partial.

alternates.naics_title: Corporate, Subsidiary, and Regional Managing Offices
alternates.justification: 'Siemens USA' is formally the regional managing organization for Siemens AG's US subsidiaries.
Siemens Digital Industries Software is a major US business publishing PLM and EDA software.
Its Smart Infrastructure unit manufactures switchgear and electrical distribution equipment in the US.

category_justification: It is the US arm of a for-profit publicly traded multinational manufacturer, commenting on its own commercial behalf.

name: Stanford CRFM, Stanford RegLab, and Stanford HAI
resolved_name: Center for Research on Foundation Models, RegLab, and Institute for Human-Centered Artificial Intelligence, Stanford University
description: This is a joint submission by three research units of Stanford University: the Center for Research on Foundation Models (CRFM), the Regulation, Evaluation, and Governance Lab (RegLab), and the Stanford Institute for Human-Centered Artificial Intelligence (HAI). CRFM studies the science and evaluation of foundation models, RegLab partners with government agencies on data-driven policy implementation, and HAI is Stanford's university-wide institute for AI research, education, and policy. All three are academic sub-units of Stanford University, and the NITRD respondent index labels the submission 'Academia'.
justification: The submitters are research centers of Stanford University, and university sub-units carrying out academic research and teaching are classified with the parent degree-granting institution.
category_justification: All three named bodies are internal centers of Stanford University, a private degree-granting research university, and the official index labels them 'Academia'.

name: Starburst
description: Starburst Data, Inc. is a private American enterprise software company headquartered in Boston, founded by contributors to the open-source Trino (formerly PrestoSQL) distributed SQL query engine. It sells commercial data lakehouse and federated analytics products, Starburst Enterprise and the managed Starburst Galaxy service, which let organizations query data across warehouses, lakes, and other sources without centralizing it, and it has extended the platform toward AI and agentic workloads. The NITRD respondent index lists it as a private-sector submitter.
justification: Starburst's primary activity is developing and licensing its own commercial data analytics software distribution built on Trino.

alternates.naics_title: Computing Infrastructure Providers, Data Processing, Web Hosting, and Related Services
alternates.justification: Starburst Galaxy is a fully managed cloud data-processing service hosted by the company.
It provides architecture and deployment services for enterprise data platforms.
Some revenue derives from customer-specific engineering and connector development.

category_justification: Starburst Data is a venture-backed for-profit software vendor filing in its own commercial capacity.

name: Stop AI
description: Stop AI is a Bay Area activist organization founded in 2024 that campaigns for a permanent ban on the development of artificial general intelligence, which it argues poses an extinction-level risk. It is known for nonviolent civil disobedience, including blockades of OpenAI's San Francisco offices that have led to arrests, alongside public outreach and petitions. It operates as a small volunteer-driven advocacy group; the NITRD respondent index lists it as a non-profit submitter.
justification: The organization's primary activity is public advocacy and protest aimed at changing policy on AI development, which is social advocacy.

alternates.justification: It functions partly as a volunteer civic group organizing members around a shared cause.
Only if it were treated as an organized body of practitioners, which it is not.
It solicits donations to fund its campaigns, but grantmaking is not its activity.

category_justification: Reporting and the NITRD index describe it as a non-profit pursuing a public-interest cause rather than a membership body representing members' collective interests, though its volunteer-activist structure sits close to the coalition/advocacy boundary.

name: Survival and Flourishing .Com, PBC
resolved_name: Survival and Flourishing Corp (dba Survival and Flourishing .Com, PBC)
description: Survival and Flourishing Corp is a US public benefit corporation that engages in philanthropy, making grants and running projects intended to improve prospects for the long-term survival and flourishing of humanity and other sentient beings. Its grants are largely funded by philanthropist Jaan Tallinn and are made mostly on recommendations produced through the affiliated Survival and Flourishing Fund process; because it is a PBC rather than a charity, it can also fund for-profit companies, and it operates direct projects such as OpenLetter.net. Its RFI response was filed under the FlexHEG (Flexible Hardware-Enabled Guarantees) hardware-based AI governance initiative, and the NITRD respondent index lists it as a private-sector submitter.
justification: Its primary activity is distributing philanthropic grants to organizations, companies, and projects, which is a grantmaking and giving service rather than an operating or investment business.

alternates.justification: It functions much like a private grantmaking foundation funded by a single principal donor, though it is not organized as a foundation.
As a corporate vehicle deploying a donor's capital, it could be read as a funding vehicle.

alternates.naics_title: All Other Professional, Scientific, and Technical Services
alternates.justification: Its direct projects, including AI governance work such as FlexHEG, are technical policy services.

category_justification: It is legally a for-profit public benefit corporation and the NITRD index labels it 'Private sector', though its sole activity is philanthropy, which makes the nonprofit category a close competing read.

name: Team Pennsylvania
description: Team Pennsylvania is a statewide nonprofit public-private partnership headquartered in Harrisburg that convenes government, business, and civic leaders around the commonwealth's long-term economic development. It is co-chaired by the Governor of Pennsylvania and a private-sector leader, and organizes its work through cross-sector collaboratives and strategic impact initiatives in agriculture, energy, manufacturing, robotics and technology, and life sciences. The organization describes itself as a neutral broker and convener that stewards blended public and private funding rather than as a government agency.
justification: Its primary activity is convening industry and government stakeholders to promote the commonwealth's business and economic development interests, which is the promotional and advocacy work covered by Business Associations.

alternates.justification: Much of its output is public-policy advocacy and strategy for economic development rather than direct services to dues-paying businesses.

alternates.naics_title: Administrative Management and General Management Consulting Services
alternates.justification: It produces strategic plans, roadmaps, and industry analyses for partners in a manner resembling management consulting.

alternates.naics_title: Other Similar Organizations (except Business, Professional, Labor, and Political Organizations)
alternates.justification: As a hybrid public-private convening body it does not fit cleanly into any single 813 subcategory.

category_justification: Its own About page and the NITRD respondent index both identify it as a nonprofit organization, and it is funded by grants and investments rather than by a dues-paying membership, though its collaborative structure gives it some coalition characteristics.

name: The Future of Free Speech, Vanderbilt
resolved_name: The Future of Free Speech (independent nonprofit think tank hosted at Vanderbilt University)
description: The Future of Free Speech is an independent, nonpartisan think tank located at Vanderbilt University and affiliated with the Dialogue Vanderbilt initiative. Founded as a collaboration between the Danish judicial think tank Justitia and Vanderbilt, it is led by executive director Jacob Mchangama, who is also a research professor at the university.
