It produces research, databases, toolkits, and advocacy on freedom of expression, including content moderation, digital regulation, disinformation, and the speech implications of artificial intelligence.
naics_title: Research and Development in the Social Sciences and Humanities
justification: Its primary output is original social-science and legal research on free expression policy, which is the defining activity of research and development in the social sciences and humanities.

alternates.justification: Freedom of expression is a civil-liberties cause and the organization engages in principled advocacy alongside its research.
It is physically housed at Vanderbilt University and the official respondent index labels it Academia.
Its policy campaigns and public commentary are general social advocacy not confined to human rights framing.

category_justification: Its own About page states it is an independent nonprofit organization rather than a Vanderbilt department, although the university hosting and the index's Academia label make a university classification arguable.

name: The Joint Commission
description: The Joint Commission is an independent, Illinois-based nonprofit organization that develops performance standards for and accredits and certifies health care organizations and programs in the United States. Its accreditation covers the large majority of US hospitals and is recognized by the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services for deemed status. It was founded by, and its corporate membership historically includes, medical and hospital professional bodies such as the American Medical Association and the American Hospital Association, but its operating work is standards-setting, on-site survey, and certification rather than member representation.
justification: It is an industry standards-development and accreditation body created and governed by health care business and professional associations, the activity grouping in which standards organizations are conventionally placed.

alternates.naics_title: All Other Professional, Scientific, and Technical Services
alternates.justification: Its day-to-day revenue activity is fee-based professional accreditation, certification, and survey services delivered to client hospitals.
Its corporate members are professional societies of physicians, surgeons, and dentists.

alternates.naics_title: Administrative Management and General Management Consulting Services
alternates.justification: Through affiliates it provides quality-improvement consulting and advisory services to health care providers.

category_justification: It is a 501(c)(3) mission-driven body whose core activity is accrediting health care organizations in the public interest rather than representing the collective interests of a dues-paying membership, and the NITRD index labels it Non-profit.

name: ThoughtLinks
description: ThoughtLinks is a private strategic advisory and consulting firm serving C-suite executives at banks and capital-markets institutions. Founded by former Bank of America technology and operations executive Sumeet Chabria, it advises clients on enterprise transformation, operating-model change, and artificial-intelligence strategy and adoption. It operates through a network of senior industry practitioners rather than a traditional large-firm consulting staff.
naics_title: Administrative Management and General Management Consulting Services
justification: Its primary activity is fee-based general management and strategy advice to executive leadership on organizational transformation, the core of administrative and general management consulting.

alternates.justification: Its focus on technology-enabled operating models in banking could be treated as a specialized management consulting niche.

alternates.naics_title: Other Scientific and Technical Consulting Services
alternates.justification: A large share of its engagements concern AI and technology architecture rather than general management.
It advises on enterprise technology and AI system design, though it does not implement systems itself.

category_justification: It is a for-profit LLC advisory firm; it commented in its own capacity, but its expertise derives from consulting engagements with unnamed banking and capital-markets clients.

name: TourScanner
description: TourScanner is a for-profit online metasearch and price-comparison platform for tours, attractions, and travel activities, founded in 2018 by Simone Semprini, Guillaume Picard, and Emily Dimucci. It aggregates more than a million offers across roughly 5,000 destinations from over 30 online travel agencies and suppliers, letting users compare and then book through partner sites. The company is fully remote, earns revenue primarily through affiliate commissions on referred bookings, and also operates mobile apps and premium products.
naics_title: All Other Travel Arrangement and Reservation Services
justification: Its primary activity is arranging travel activity bookings by aggregating and routing customers to reservation providers, which falls under travel arrangement and reservation services not classified as an agency or tour operator.

alternates.naics_title: Web Search Portals and All Other Information Services
alternates.justification: It functions technically as a vertical search portal that indexes third-party inventory and monetizes referrals rather than selling travel itself.
It acts as an intermediary between travelers and activity suppliers on a commission basis, much like an online travel agency.
Its entire catalog consists of tours and guided activities, though it does not assemble or operate them.

category_justification: It is a venture-style for-profit travel technology company with paying commercial partners, and the NITRD index lists it as Private sector.

name: Transluce
description: Transluce is a nonprofit artificial-intelligence research lab co-founded in 2024 by Jacob Steinhardt, who took leave from UC Berkeley, and Sarah Schwettmann. It builds open-source, scalable tools and investigator agents for understanding, auditing, and interpreting the behavior of AI systems. Its stated mission is to steer AI systems in the public interest by making their internal behavior legible to researchers, developers, and the public.
naics_title: Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology)
justification: Its primary activity is original computer-science and engineering research on AI interpretability and evaluation, which falls under R&D in the physical and engineering sciences.

alternates.justification: It releases open-source interpretability tools and agent software as a major output of its work.

alternates.naics_title: Research and Development in the Social Sciences and Humanities
alternates.justification: Part of its work concerns AI governance, oversight, and the public interest rather than pure technical research.
Building investigator agents and analysis pipelines involves substantial software engineering.

category_justification: It publicly launched and is consistently described by its founders and UC Berkeley as a nonprofit research lab with a public-interest mission and no membership base, notwithstanding the index's Private sector label.

name: Travel Lemming
description: Travel Lemming is a for-profit online travel media publication founded in 2016 by Nate Hake, based in Denver, Colorado. It publishes destination guides, reviews, and travel advice written by a distributed team of writers and editors, reaching millions of readers annually. Its revenue comes primarily from advertising and affiliate partnerships tied to its published content, and it has publicly engaged on how AI-generated search results affect independent publishers.
justification: Its primary activity is publishing an ongoing, editorially produced online travel magazine of articles and guides, which 2022 NAICS places with periodical publishers regardless of internet-only distribution.

alternates.naics_title: Media Streaming Distribution Services, Social Networks, and Other Media Networks and Content Providers
alternates.justification: As a web-native content provider it may be classified with other online media and content providers rather than as a periodical.

alternates.naics_title: Web Search Portals and All Other Information Services
alternates.justification: Its site functions substantially as a searchable travel information resource monetized through referrals.
A large share of its revenue derives from advertising and affiliate marketing placements.

category_justification: It is a founder-owned commercial publishing business monetized through advertising and affiliate revenue, and the NITRD index lists it as Private sector.

name: True Ventures
description: True Ventures is a US venture capital firm, based in the San Francisco Bay Area, that invests primarily at the seed and early stage in technology companies. It raises and manages a series of limited partnership funds and has backed companies including Fitbit, Peloton, Ring, and Duo Security. Its business consists of deploying committed capital into startups and supporting portfolio founders in exchange for equity and management fees and carried interest.
justification: Its primary activity is acting as a venture capital company that pools investor capital and takes equity positions in private companies, the activity classified under miscellaneous intermediation.

alternates.justification: The management company manages pooled funds on behalf of limited partners for a fee, which is portfolio management.
Its fund administration and investor services activities fall under residual financial investment activities.
The underlying limited partnership funds themselves are pooled investment vehicles.

category_justification: It is a for-profit private venture capital partnership investing on behalf of limited partners, and the NITRD index lists it as Private sector.

name: Trustible
description: Trustible is a venture-backed Arlington, Virginia software company that sells an AI governance platform to regulated enterprises. Its subscription product inventories an organization's AI systems and models, scores them for risk, and maps them to regulatory frameworks such as the EU AI Act and the NIST AI Risk Management Framework. The company is an independent for-profit startup and publishes AI policy research alongside its commercial product.
justification: Trustible's primary activity is developing and licensing a proprietary AI governance software platform on a subscription basis, which is the defining activity of software publishing.

alternates.naics_title: Computing Infrastructure Providers, Data Processing, Web Hosting, and Related Services
alternates.justification: The platform is delivered as a hosted cloud service, which some SaaS vendors are coded under.
Deployments involve integrating the governance platform with a client's existing AI and IT systems.

alternates.naics_title: Other Scientific and Technical Consulting Services
alternates.justification: The company also provides AI regulatory and risk advisory content to customers.

category_justification: Trustible is a privately held venture-funded for-profit vendor, and the RFI respondent index lists it as 'Private sector'.

name: Twilio
description: Twilio Inc. is a publicly traded San Francisco-based customer engagement company whose APIs let developers embed messaging, voice, email, and video into their own applications. It pioneered the communications platform-as-a-service (CPaaS) model and has extended it with a customer data platform and AI-driven engagement tools. The company sells to businesses on a usage and subscription basis and operates worldwide.
justification: Twilio's primary activity is designing and licensing proprietary communications and customer-engagement software APIs, which it markets as products rather than operating a telecommunications network of its own.

alternates.justification: Twilio resells and routes SMS and voice traffic, a telecommunications service activity.

alternates.naics_title: Computing Infrastructure Providers, Data Processing, Web Hosting, and Related Services
alternates.justification: Its APIs run as a hosted cloud platform processing customer message and profile data.
Twilio buys carrier capacity wholesale and resells it to application developers.

category_justification: Twilio is a for-profit NYSE-listed corporation (ticker TWLO) and is labeled 'Private sector' in the RFI respondent index.

name: UC San Diego Heath/UC San Francisco Health
resolved_name: UC San Diego Health and UCSF Health (academic health systems of the University of California)
description: UC San Diego Health and UCSF Health are the academic health systems owned and operated by the Regents of the University of California at its San Diego and San Francisco campuses. Each runs teaching hospitals, outpatient clinics, and physician groups while supporting the medical education and clinical research missions of its campus. The two filed a joint response to the AI Action Plan RFI reflecting their shared work on clinical AI deployment and governance.
justification: The named entities are the hospital and clinical care enterprises of the two campuses, whose primary activity is operating general acute-care academic medical centers.

alternates.justification: Both are integral units of degree-granting University of California campuses and carry out teaching missions.

alternates.naics_title: Offices of Physicians (except Mental Health Specialists)
alternates.justification: Each system includes large employed faculty physician practices delivering ambulatory care.

alternates.naics_title: Specialty (except Psychiatric and Substance Abuse) Hospitals
alternates.justification: Both operate specialty facilities such as cancer and children's hospitals within the system.

category_justification: Both are owned and operated by the Regents of the University of California as campus academic health centers rather than as independent nonprofits, and the RFI index labels the submission 'Academia'; a 'nonprofit' reading is possible but they are not separately incorporated charities.

name: UVA
resolved_name: University of Virginia (submission led by the Sloane Lab)
description: UVA is the University of Virginia, a public research university in Charlottesville founded in 1819 and governed by a Board of Visitors. Its RFI submission was organized through the Sloane Lab in the School of Data Science and co-signed by faculty at Santa Clara University, Barnard College/Columbia, Harvard, and Stanford, addressing sensors and materiality in AI systems. The institution grants undergraduate, graduate, and professional degrees and conducts sponsored research across disciplines.
justification: The University of Virginia's primary activity is granting baccalaureate and higher degrees as a public research university, which is exactly this code.

alternates.naics_title: Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology)
alternates.justification: The submission came from a sponsored research lab whose output is engineering and computing research.

alternates.naics_title: Research and Development in the Social Sciences and Humanities
alternates.justification: The Sloane Lab's work is sociotechnical, spanning data science and media studies.

alternates.naics_title: Other Scientific and Technical Consulting Services
alternates.justification: The comment functions as expert technical advice to a federal agency.

category_justification: The respondent name is the University of Virginia itself, a degree-granting public university, and the RFI index labels the submission 'Academia'.

name: Ultrapass
description: UltraPass Identity Corp is a private US company that builds a digital identity and age-verification platform using biometrics, verifiable credentials, and its UAuth protocol. Its products let websites, app stores, and regulated merchants confirm a user's age or identity without retaining underlying personal documents. The company markets itself as privacy-preserving and interoperable and engages in policy debates over online age assurance.
justification: The company's primary activity is developing and licensing proprietary identity and age-verification software and protocols to business customers.

alternates.naics_title: Computing Infrastructure Providers, Data Processing, Web Hosting, and Related Services
alternates.justification: Identity verification is delivered as a hosted service that processes credential and biometric data on behalf of clients.
Age and identity screening performed for other businesses can be treated as an outsourced business support service.
Customer deployments require integrating the identity platform into existing systems.

category_justification: UltraPass Identity Corp is a for-profit venture-stage corporation and the RFI index labels the submitter 'Private sector'.

name: Utah Responsible AI Community Consortium
resolved_name: Responsible AI Community Consortium, One-U Responsible AI Initiative, University of Utah
description: The Responsible AI Community Consortium is a multi-stakeholder membership body convened and hosted by the University of Utah's One-U Responsible AI Initiative at the Scientific Computing and Imaging Institute. It brings together academic, industry, government, and community members, with core and community membership tiers, and works through special interest groups on infrastructure, policy, workforce, and community engagement. It produces collective outputs such as an AI leadership blueprint for the state and meets monthly.
justification: Its primary activity is convening dues- and resource-contributing member organizations to advance shared positions on responsible AI, which is association activity rather than direct service delivery.

alternates.justification: The consortium's community-engagement pillar and open community membership tier resemble a civic organization.
It is hosted and administered inside the University of Utah, so its activity could be attributed to the university.
Much of its membership consists of AI practitioners and researchers organized by professional interest.

category_justification: The consortium's own site describes tiered membership across academia, industry, government, and community organizations working through special interest groups, making it a membership-based multi-stakeholder coalition despite the RFI index's 'Non-federal government' label.

name: Utilidata
description: Utilidata is a Providence, Rhode Island for-profit company that develops distributed artificial intelligence software for electric utility grids. Its Karman platform, built on an NVIDIA-based module embedded in smart meters, runs machine learning at the grid edge to support real-time voltage optimization, outage detection, and EV and DER management. It is venture-backed and sells to utilities and meter manufacturers rather than serving retail electricity customers.
justification: Utilidata's primary activity is developing and licensing proprietary distributed AI software for grid devices, with hardware serving as the delivery vehicle for that software.

alternates.naics_title: Instruments and Related Products Manufacturing for Measuring, Displaying, and Controlling Industrial Process Variables
alternates.justification: The Karman module is an embedded metering and grid-control device produced with hardware partners.
Utility deployments involve substantial custom software work for each client.
The company performs power-systems engineering analysis for distribution utilities.

category_justification: Utilidata is a venture-funded for-profit technology company (Series C investors include NVIDIA) and the RFI index labels it 'Private sector'.

name: VAST Federal
resolved_name: VAST Federal (public sector division of VAST Data, Inc.)
description: VAST Federal is the US public sector arm of VAST Data, Inc., a for-profit data platform company headquartered in New York. It sells VAST's software-defined data platform, which unifies storage, database, and AI data pipeline services on commodity flash hardware, to defense, intelligence, and civilian federal agencies. It handles federal contracting, security accreditation, and cleared support for the parent company's products.
justification: VAST's core product is a software-defined data platform licensed to customers, and the federal division's primary activity is selling and supporting that software for government use.

alternates.naics_title: Computing Infrastructure Providers, Data Processing, Web Hosting, and Related Services
alternates.justification: The platform is sold as AI data infrastructure, including consumption-based and cloud-delivered forms.

alternates.naics_title: Computer and Computer Peripheral Equipment and Software Merchant Wholesalers
alternates.justification: The federal division largely resells the parent's appliances and software through government channels and resellers.
VAST's platform is frequently delivered as branded flash storage appliances.

category_justification: VAST Federal is a wholly owned commercial division of the for-profit VAST Data, Inc. serving government customers, and the RFI index labels it 'Private sector'.

name: VEIR
description: VEIR is a venture-backed US company developing high-temperature superconducting overhead electric transmission line systems that carry five to ten times the power of conventional conductors at the same voltage. Its core product combines superconducting conductor assemblies with a proprietary passive open-loop liquid-nitrogen cooling system, demonstrated at outdoor test facilities in Massachusetts and in collaboration with National Grid. The company raised roughly $75 million to pilot its transmission technology for grid operators and data center interconnection.
naics_title: Other Communication and Energy Wire Manufacturing
justification: VEIR's primary output is a superconducting power transmission conductor and cable system, which falls under manufacturing of energy wire and cable rather than a service activity.

alternates.naics_title: Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology)
alternates.justification: The company is still largely pre-commercial and its dominant expenditure is engineering research and demonstration of superconducting transmission technology.

alternates.naics_title: All Other Miscellaneous Electrical Equipment and Component Manufacturing
alternates.justification: The cryogenic cooling and termination hardware around the conductor is miscellaneous electrical equipment not captured by the wire code.

alternates.naics_title: Power, Distribution, and Specialty Transformer Manufacturing
alternates.justification: The product is sold into the same electric power transmission equipment market, though VEIR does not manufacture transformers.

category_justification: VEIR is a privately held for-profit company that has raised venture capital and is listed as 'Private sector' in the NITRD RFI respondent index.

name: Vanta
description: Vanta is a US for-profit software company that sells a cloud-based trust and security compliance automation platform. Its product continuously monitors a customer's systems and collects evidence to support audits and certifications such as SOC 2, ISO 27001, HIPAA, PCI DSS, and GDPR. Founded in 2018 and headquartered in San Francisco, it serves thousands of business customers on a subscription basis.
justification: Vanta's primary activity is developing and licensing its own proprietary compliance-automation software product on a subscription basis, which is the defining activity of a software publisher.

alternates.naics_title: Computing Infrastructure Providers, Data Processing, Web Hosting, and Related Services
alternates.justification: The platform is delivered as a hosted multi-tenant service that continuously ingests and processes customer system data.
Vanta supports customers in configuring security controls and integrating monitoring across their systems.
Continuous security control monitoring could be read as an ongoing computer-related service rather than a packaged product.

category_justification: Vanta is a venture-funded for-profit software vendor selling subscriptions, and the RFI index labels it 'Private sector'.

name: Veriten
description: Veriten is an independent, employee-owned research, strategy, and investment firm focused on the intersection of energy, power, and technology, based in Houston, Texas. It publishes recurring research and media programs including the 'C.O.B. Tuesday' and 'Super-Spiked' series, and provides strategic advisory work to energy and power organizations. It also manages an energy investment fund, NexTen, launched in 2023 by founder Maynard Holt and partner Arjun Murti.
naics_title: Other Scientific and Technical Consulting Services
justification: Veriten's primary revenue-generating activity is subscription energy-sector research and technical strategic advisory to industry clients, which fits scientific and technical consulting.

alternates.justification: Veriten manages the NexTen energy investment fund and deploys capital on behalf of investors.
Its strategic advisory work with energy companies is general business strategy consulting rather than technical engineering advice.

alternates.naics_title: Web Search Portals and All Other Information Services
alternates.justification: A large share of its public output is distributed research content, podcasts, and market commentary.

category_justification: Veriten self-describes as an independent employee-owned for-profit research, strategy, and investment firm, and the RFI index lists it as 'Private sector'.

name: Vermillio
description: Vermillio is a US for-profit AI company whose TraceID platform detects unauthorized AI-generated use of an individual's or rights holder's name, image, likeness, and copyrighted works, and supports authenticated licensing of those rights. Its customers and partners include the talent agency WME and the Association of American Publishers, and it was named to the 2025 TIME100 Most Influential Companies list. The company raised a $16 million Series A to expand its AI licensing and protection platform.
justification: Vermillio's primary activity is developing and licensing the proprietary TraceID software platform to rights holders on a subscription basis.

alternates.naics_title: Web Search Portals and All Other Information Services
alternates.justification: TraceID continuously scans the open web and indexes matches, which is an information-search and monitoring service.
The detection and takedown workflow could be characterized as a managed computer-related service rather than a packaged product.

alternates.naics_title: All Other Professional, Scientific, and Technical Services
alternates.justification: Its rights-licensing brokerage for talent and publishers is a professional service not otherwise classified.

category_justification: Vermillio is a venture-funded for-profit technology company with commercial customers, listed as 'Private sector' in the RFI index.

name: WalletHub
description: WalletHub is a US for-profit personal finance website operated by Evolution Finance, Inc. and headquartered in Washington, DC. It offers free consumer credit scores and credit report monitoring, comparison tools and reviews for credit cards, loans, and insurance, and publishes widely cited data-driven rankings and studies. Its revenue comes primarily from advertising and affiliate referrals when users apply for financial products through the site.
naics_title: Web Search Portals and All Other Information Services
justification: WalletHub's primary activity is operating a consumer-facing web portal that aggregates and publishes financial product information, reviews, and rankings, monetized through advertising and referrals.

alternates.justification: A core free product is consumer credit score and credit report monitoring drawn from bureau data.
The site earns referral fees for routing consumers to credit card and loan issuers, resembling brokerage of credit products.
WalletHub also publishes consumer mobile applications for credit and budgeting.

category_justification: WalletHub is the consumer brand of the for-profit firm Evolution Finance, Inc., and the RFI index labels the submitter 'Private sector'.

name: William AI
description: The RFI respondent 'William AI' filed a short comment consisting of policy recommendations and quotations from Elon Musk, with no letterhead, organizational self-description, or contact affiliation. The NITRD respondent index classifies the submission as 'Individual' and assigns it a generic numbered document identifier rather than a named organizational filing. A separate, unrelated legal-technology company also trades under the name William AI, but nothing in the submission ties the comment to that firm.
justification: No commercial or institutional activity can be attributed to this respondent, so the household code is used as a placeholder for an apparent private individual rather than as a positive industry assignment.

alternates.justification: The submission is purely advocacy content urging particular AI policy outcomes.
If the respondent is in fact the similarly named legal-technology company, its product is licensed AI software.
Under the same alternative reading, the firm builds AI-based document and contract analysis tooling for legal clients.

category_justification: Two converging signals point to a private person - the official NITRD index labels the submission 'Individual' and the filing itself contains no organizational identity - but a same-named legal-tech company leaves genuine residual doubt.

name: Windborne Systems
description: WindBorne Systems is a for-profit US company in Redwood Shores, California that designs and operates a constellation of long-duration, altitude-controlling smart weather balloons that gather atmospheric profiles worldwide. It combines this proprietary observational data with deep-learning models to produce its WeatherMesh global weather forecasts, which it sells to commercial and government customers. Its partners and customers include NOAA, the US Air Force and Navy, ECMWF, and energy trading and utility firms.
naics_title: All Other Professional, Scientific, and Technical Services
justification: WindBorne's primary commercial output is weather forecasting and atmospheric data services, and weather forecasting services are indexed to this residual professional and technical services code.

alternates.naics_title: Web Search Portals and All Other Information Services
alternates.justification: Much of what it sells is access to a proprietary atmospheric and forecast data feed, which is an information service.

alternates.naics_title: Other Measuring and Controlling Device Manufacturing
alternates.justification: The company manufactures its own balloon-borne atmospheric sensing instruments in-house.

alternates.naics_title: Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology)
alternates.justification: A substantial share of its work is government-funded atmospheric science and AI forecast model research.

category_justification: WindBorne is a venture-funded for-profit company selling forecasting products and holding government contracts, listed as 'Private sector' in the RFI index.

name: Wolters Kluwer
description: Wolters Kluwer is a publicly traded Dutch multinational headquartered in Alphen aan den Rijn that supplies information, software, and services to legal, tax and accounting, healthcare, finance, and compliance professionals. It operates through five divisions - Legal & Regulatory, Tax & Accounting, Health, Financial & Corporate Compliance, and Corporate Performance & ESG - with brands including UpToDate, CCH, Enablon, and Lippincott. Expert software and digital information solutions now generate the majority of its roughly six billion euro annual revenue, well ahead of its legacy print publishing.
justification: The majority of Wolters Kluwer's revenue now comes from proprietary expert software and digital workflow solutions licensed to professionals, which is a software publishing activity.

alternates.justification: The company remains a large publisher of legal, tax, and medical reference content in digital and print form.

alternates.naics_title: Web Search Portals and All Other Information Services
alternates.justification: Products such as UpToDate and CCH are searchable subscription information databases rather than installed software.
Its Lippincott and legal treatise imprints continue to publish professional and medical books.

category_justification: Wolters Kluwer is a for-profit corporation listed on Euronext Amsterdam and is labeled 'Private sector' in the RFI respondent index.

name: Encode
description: Encode is a US nonprofit advocacy organization, founded in 2020 by Sneha Revanur and registered as a 501(c)(4), that campaigns for public-interest regulation of artificial intelligence. It works on federal and state AI legislation, coalition-building, and public campaigns, and has been involved in measures such as California's SB 53, New York's RAISE Act, and the federal TAKE IT DOWN Act. It is staffed from offices in Washington DC, California, and Boston, and is funded by individual donors and foundations rather than AI companies.
justification: Encode's primary activity is organized public advocacy and lobbying to shape AI policy on behalf of a social cause, which is the defining activity of Other Social Advocacy Organizations.

alternates.justification: Much of Encode's framing concerns civil rights and harms to individuals from AI, which could place it in the human rights advocacy subcategory.
Its origins as a youth-led civic movement give it some characteristics of a civic organization.

alternates.naics_title: Research and Development in the Social Sciences and Humanities
alternates.justification: It publishes policy analysis and research briefs, though this is supporting rather than primary activity.

category_justification: Its own site and IRS status identify it as a 501(c)(4) nonprofit with a staffed public-interest mission and no dues-paying membership base.

name: Engineering & Research International
description: Engineering & Research International (ERI) is the name used by a group of affiliated for-profit engineering firms specializing in engineering geosciences, including geotechnical investigation, materials and soil testing laboratories, surveying, and specialty contracting. The group is headquartered in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, with offices elsewhere in the Middle East as well as operations in the United States and Lebanon. Several unrelated US firms use closely similar names, so the identification of the specific commenting entity is not fully certain.
justification: The best-matching entity's primary activity is applying engineering knowledge to geotechnical, structural, and infrastructure projects for clients, which is squarely Engineering Services.

alternates.justification: A large share of ERI's business is soil, rock, concrete, asphalt, and steel materials testing laboratories.

alternates.naics_title: Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology)
alternates.justification: The 'Research' in the name could indicate a contract engineering R&D firm, which is a common profile for federal RFI commenters.

alternates.naics_title: Other Scientific and Technical Consulting Services
alternates.justification: If the entity chiefly sells technical advisory work rather than licensed engineering design, this residual consulting code would apply.

category_justification: Every organization found under this name is a for-profit engineering and testing firm serving paying clients, though which one submitted the comment could not be pinned down.

name: Engineering Biology Research Consortium
description: The Engineering Biology Research Consortium (EBRC) is a nonprofit public-private partnership, incorporated as a California public benefit corporation with 501(c)(3) status, that convenes academic and industry participants working in synthetic and engineering biology. It grew out of the NSF-funded Synthetic Biology Engineering Research Center (SynBERC) and is governed by a board drawn from universities and companies. Its main programs are technical research roadmapping, workforce education, biosecurity work, and policy and international engagement, including collaboration with NIST on AI-biosecurity safety tools.
naics_title: Research and Development in Biotechnology (except Nanobiotechnology)
justification: EBRC's core output is coordinated biotechnology research agenda-setting and technical roadmapping in engineering biology, placing its primary activity in biotechnology R&D.

alternates.justification: It functions largely as a convening body for scientists and member institutions, similar to a scientific professional society.

alternates.naics_title: Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology)
alternates.justification: Its engineering-biology scope spans engineering and life sciences R&D more broadly than biotechnology alone.
Its industry membership and sector policy advocacy resemble an industry association.

category_justification: EBRC is explicitly membership-based, with academic, industry, international, and individual council members whose collective interests it represents in roadmapping and policy engagement.

name: Entomological Soceity of America
description: The Entomological Society of America is the largest professional membership society for insect scientists, founded in 1889 and headquartered in Annapolis, Maryland. It serves roughly 7,000 members from academia, government, and industry through annual meetings, peer-reviewed journals, and the Board Certified Entomologist credentialing program. It also engages in science policy advocacy on behalf of the entomological profession. (The input name contains a misspelling of 'Society'.)
justification: ESA is a dues-based membership society that advances the professional interests of entomologists through meetings, publications, and certification, which is exactly what Professional Organizations covers.
category_justification: Its defining feature is a dues-paying professional membership whose collective scientific and policy interests it represents.

name: Enzai
description: Enzai is a venture-backed technology company that sells an enterprise AI governance, risk, and compliance software platform. Founded in Belfast with a US presence in New York, it raised seed funding from investors including Seedcamp and offers tooling for AI inventory, risk assessment, policy enforcement, and regulatory mapping against frameworks such as the EU AI Act and the NIST AI RMF. Its platform integrates with enterprise machine learning stacks including IBM watsonx.
justification: Enzai's primary activity is designing and licensing its own proprietary AI governance software product to enterprise customers, which is publishing software.

alternates.justification: Deployment and integration of the governance platform into client environments involves substantial systems design and configuration work.

alternates.naics_title: Computing Infrastructure Providers, Data Processing, Web Hosting, and Related Services
alternates.justification: The product is delivered as a hosted SaaS service, which can fall under data processing and hosting services.

alternates.naics_title: Administrative Management and General Management Consulting Services
alternates.justification: Its governance and compliance advisory content resembles management consulting, though the software is the revenue product.

category_justification: Enzai is a privately held, venture-funded for-profit software vendor selling to enterprise customers.

name: Equity and Access in Algorithms, Mechanisms, and Optimization
resolved_name: Equity and Access in Algorithms, Mechanisms, and Optimization (EAAMO), fiscally sponsored by The Hack Foundation
description: EAAMO is an interdisciplinary research community, successor to the Mechanism Design for Social Good (MD4SG) initiative, that brings together researchers and practitioners applying algorithms, optimization, and mechanism design to problems facing marginalized communities. It runs the annual ACM EAAMO conference, a colloquium series, and the year-round EAAMO Bridges working-group program, drawing participants from more than 130 institutions across some 50 countries. It has no independent corporate form and is fiscally sponsored by The Hack Foundation, a 501(c)(3), with support from ACM SIGAI and the Sloan and MacArthur foundations.
justification: Its primary activity is convening a scholarly community through conferences, colloquia, and working groups, the characteristic function of a professional or learned society.

alternates.naics_title: Research and Development in the Social Sciences and Humanities
alternates.justification: Its substantive output is interdisciplinary social-science and computational research on equity and access.
As a volunteer-run community organized around a social mission it partly resembles a civic organization.

alternates.naics_title: Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology)
alternates.justification: Much of the underlying work is computer science and optimization research, which falls under engineering and physical sciences R&D.

category_justification: It operates under 501(c)(3) fiscal sponsorship by The Hack Foundation and pursues a public-interest research mission rather than representing dues-paying members' collective interests, though its large open community edges toward a professional association.

name: Eugene Neelou Alex Polyakov, Adversa AI
resolved_name: Adversa AI (comment submitted by Eugene Neelou and Alex Polyakov)
description: Adversa AI is a for-profit, venture-backed AI security company whose work covers adversarial machine learning research, AI red teaming engagements for enterprises, and a runtime security platform for AI coding agents. It was co-founded by Alex Polyakov, an offensive-security researcher, and the submission is attributed to him together with Eugene Neelou, the firm's AI safety and security lead. The company has published research on adversarial AI and has previously filed comments with NIST on AI risk management.
justification: Adversa AI's primary revenue activity is delivering AI security testing, red teaming, and system-hardening engagements for client computer systems, which falls under computer systems design services.

alternates.justification: The company is commercializing a proprietary runtime security platform product, which would make it a software publisher.
Standalone security testing and red teaming services that are not systems design proper fall into this residual computer services code.

alternates.naics_title: Other Scientific and Technical Consulting Services
alternates.justification: Its adversarial AI advisory and threat research work can be read as specialized technical consulting.

category_justification: Adversa AI is a privately held, VC-funded for-profit security vendor, and the two named individuals are its executives commenting in that capacity.

name: Event Education and Workforce Development Federation
description: The Events Education & Workforce Development Federation is a US nonprofit federation created to connect, support, and professionalize the workforce of the live events and exhibitions industry. It runs mentorship, apprenticeship, training, and career-pathway programs across event industry verticals and advocates for formal recognition of event work as a defined career field. It is governed by a board of directors with an advisory council and education committee, and partners with allied industry associations, employers, and technology sponsors.
justification: Its primary activity is acting as an industry-wide federation that promotes the collective interests, standards, and recognition of the events business and its workforce.

alternates.justification: A large part of its program work is delivering training, mentorship, and professional development to event industry workers.
If its base is individual event professionals rather than member firms, it functions as a professional society.
Its career guidance, curriculum, and educational resource work is a form of educational support service.

category_justification: It is structured as a federation of event-industry stakeholders and allied associations whose stated purpose is advancing the sector's collective workforce interests and industry recognition.

name: Workforce AI
description: Workforce AI Corp is a for-profit US technology startup, registered in Sheridan, Wyoming and led by CEO Mario Costanz, that sells an artificial intelligence platform under the HireWorkforce.ai brand. Its product deploys video-avatar "digital employees" that automate routine administrative tasks such as IT helpdesk support, HR inquiries, research assistance, and customer service for enterprise and government customers. Its comment to the NITRD AI Action Plan RFI promoted human-centric AI that augments federal workers rather than replacing them, and the official respondent index lists it as a Private sector respondent.
justification: Its primary activity is developing and licensing a proprietary AI software platform of conversational digital-worker agents sold as a subscription product, which is software design, publication, and distribution.

alternates.justification: If digital-employee deployments are substantially built and integrated per client rather than sold as a packaged product, the work is custom programming.

alternates.naics_title: Computing Infrastructure Providers, Data Processing, Web Hosting, and Related Services
alternates.justification: The platform is delivered as a hosted cloud service, which can place a SaaS AI vendor in application hosting and data processing.
The company stresses integration with existing government systems, an activity associated with systems design and integration services.

category_justification: Its own RFI submission identifies it as Workforce AI Corp with a CEO and a commercial product website, and the NITRD respondent index labels it Private sector.

name: ZealStrat
description: ZealStrat LLC is a privately held US consulting firm that advises businesses on AI ethics, responsible AI adoption, and broader business and market strategy. Its stated service lines are ethical AI consulting, predictive market research, and enterprise solutions, and it also runs the ZealStrat Academy offering IEEE CertifAIEd training plus a "Sightwise" insights publication. It submitted a comment to the NITRD AI Action Plan RFI and appears in the official respondent index as a Private sector respondent.
naics_title: Administrative Management and General Management Consulting Services
justification: Its primary activity is fee-based advisory work on AI governance, ethics, and business strategy for client organizations, which is general management and strategic planning consulting rather than software production.

alternates.justification: The AI ethics and responsible-AI specialization is a niche advisory practice that can fall outside general management consulting.

alternates.naics_title: Marketing Research and Public Opinion Polling
alternates.justification: Predictive market research is one of its three named solution areas and would be coded here if it dominated revenue.
The ZealStrat Academy delivers certification training courses, a distinct professional development training activity.

category_justification: It is an LLC operating a commercial consulting and paid-training practice, and the NITRD respondent index labels it Private sector.

name: iProov
description: iProov Limited is a privately held London-headquartered technology company, founded in 2011 by Andrew Bud, that develops biometric face verification and liveness-detection technology. Its cloud-delivered products, including Genuine Presence Assurance and Face Verifier, authenticate that a remote user is the right person, a real person, and authenticating in real time, and are used by government agencies, banks, and healthcare organizations for onboarding and passwordless authentication. It filed a comment on the NITRD AI Action Plan RFI addressing deepfake and identity-fraud threats, and the official respondent index lists it as a Private sector respondent.
justification: Its primary activity is developing and licensing proprietary biometric verification software and SDKs to enterprise and government customers, which is software publishing.

alternates.naics_title: Computing Infrastructure Providers, Data Processing, Web Hosting, and Related Services
alternates.justification: Verification is performed as a hosted cloud transaction service, so the revenue could be classified as data processing and hosted services.
Deployments involve integrating the biometric service into client identity systems, an activity coded as systems design and integration.
Identity assurance delivered as an ongoing computer-related security service fits this residual category if it is not treated as a packaged software product.

category_justification: iProov is a venture-backed for-profit private limited company selling commercial biometric products, and the NITRD respondent index labels it Private sector.

name: promptheory.com
resolved_name: promptheory.com (unidentified; submitter-supplied organization field on an individual comment)
description: The submission recorded under "promptheory.com" is an anonymous public comment filed through regulations.gov to the NSF docket for the AI Action Plan RFI, with no submitter name or email and only this web address typed into the organization field. The domain does not resolve to any live website and no company, nonprofit, or other registered entity of this name could be located in web research. The comment itself is an unsourced opinion piece arguing that AI development and hiring should be opened beyond computer scientists to ordinary users and workers, and the official NITRD respondent index classifies the respondent type as Individual.
naics_title: Web Search Portals and All Other Information Services
justification: No verifiable operating entity or primary activity exists behind the name, so the only weak basis for a code is that the string is a website domain, which would fall under other information services.

alternates.justification: The comment is purely policy advocacy, which is how an unaffiliated advocacy voice would be coded if it were an organization.
The name suggests an AI prompt-related software or content project, which if operating would most likely be programming services.
A one-person AI prompting practice marketed via a domain name would most plausibly be a niche consulting operation.

category_justification: The NITRD respondent index labels this submission's respondent type Individual, the submitter left name and email blank, and the text is a first-person opinion comment with no organization behind it.

name: Everfox
resolved_name: Everfox (formerly Forcepoint Federal; portfolio company of TPG)
description: Everfox is a U.S. cybersecurity company that builds defense-grade security software for federal government, defense, and intelligence customers. Its product portfolio centers on cross domain solutions such as High Speed Guard and Trusted Thin Client, plus insider risk management and content sanitization tools. It was carved out of Forcepoint and rebranded from Forcepoint Federal to Everfox in January 2024 under owner TPG.
justification: Everfox's primary activity is developing and licensing packaged cybersecurity software products (cross domain guards, insider threat tooling) to government customers, which is software publishing.

alternates.justification: Much of its federal work involves deploying and integrating secure system architectures for agency environments.
It also supplies managed and professional cybersecurity services around its products.

alternates.naics_title: Computing Infrastructure Providers, Data Processing, Web Hosting, and Related Services
alternates.justification: Some offerings are delivered as hosted or cloud-based secure computing services.

category_justification: Everfox is a for-profit, privately held cybersecurity vendor owned by the investment firm TPG and selling products under contract to government buyers.

name: FWD.us
description: FWD.us is a U.S. advocacy organization founded in 2013 by Mark Zuckerberg, Joe Green, and other technology and business leaders. Organized primarily as a 501(c)(4) social welfare group with an affiliated 501(c)(3) arm, it lobbies and runs public campaigns on immigration reform and criminal justice reform. Its work includes grassroots organizing, research, advertising, and coalition-building with policymakers in Washington, D.C. and the states.
justification: Its primary activity is advocating and lobbying for immigration and criminal justice policy change on behalf of a social cause, which is the core of Other Social Advocacy Organizations.

alternates.justification: As a 501(c)(4) that lobbies and runs political advertising, it overlaps with political organization activity.
Its immigration and incarceration work is framed substantially in civil and human rights terms.
It functions as a civic membership vehicle for its founding business leaders.

category_justification: FWD.us was formed as a bipartisan coalition of named technology and business leaders who fund and are publicly listed with the group, and it exists to press their collective policy agenda rather than to deliver services; the 'nonprofit' category expressly excludes membership and advocacy bodies.

name: Figure Eight Federal
resolved_name: Figure Eight Federal (FOCI-mitigated U.S. federal affiliate of Appen Limited)
description: Figure Eight Federal is an Arlington, Virginia contractor that supplies AI and machine learning data services to U.S. defense, intelligence, and health agencies. Its Artemis platform handles data labeling and annotation, training-data pipelines, and human-in-the-loop model development for specialized sources such as synthetic aperture radar, LiDAR, and multispectral imagery. It operates as the FOCI-mitigated (foreign ownership, control, or influence) U.S. arm associated with Appen Limited so it can hold cleared government work.
justification: Its primary activity is designing, integrating, and operating AI/ML data and model-development systems for federal agency customers under contract.

alternates.naics_title: Computing Infrastructure Providers, Data Processing, Web Hosting, and Related Services
alternates.justification: Large-scale data annotation and training-data pipeline work is a form of data processing service.
The Artemis annotation platform is a licensed software product in its own right.
It performs bespoke model and pipeline development tailored to individual agency missions.

category_justification: It is a for-profit government contractor tied to the publicly listed firm Appen, selling AI data services commercially.

name: For Every Child
description: Research could not confirm which entity submitted under the name 'For Every Child.' The phrase is used by several distinct organizations, including UNICEF's global tagline, EveryChild of the Quad Cities (foreverychild.org), and various child-welfare nonprofits, and no submission record could be tied to any one of them. Its sector, legal form, and primary activity therefore remain unverified.
justification: The name suggests a child-focused advocacy or welfare mission, but the entity could not be identified, so this code is a low-confidence placeholder rather than a verified match.

alternates.justification: If the submitter is a direct-service child welfare agency, this would be the fitting code.
Several organizations using this name are grantmaking foundations supporting children's causes.
It may be a civic or community membership group organized around children's issues.

category_justification: Multiple unrelated organizations use this name and no evidence tied the comment to a specific one, so the entity type cannot be confirmed.

name: Frederick County
resolved_name: Frederick County, Maryland (county government, Office of the County Executive)
description: Frederick County is a chartered county government in the U.S. state of Maryland, seated in the City of Frederick. It operates under a charter form of government with an elected County Executive and a seven-member County Council, and delivers services including planning and zoning, public works, health and human services, libraries, and economic development. Its AI Action Plan comment was submitted by County Executive Jessica Fitzwater through the Office of the County Executive.
justification: Frederick County is a general-purpose local government combining an elected executive and a legislative council, which is exactly what this code covers.

alternates.justification: The comment came specifically from the Office of the County Executive, a local chief-executive office.
Some county administrative functions fall under general government support activities.
The County Council is the county's legislative body and could anchor the classification.

category_justification: The submission is on Frederick County Government letterhead signed by the elected County Executive, making this a local (county) government body in Maryland.

name: Frontier Model Forum
description: The Frontier Model Forum is an industry body launched in July 2023 by Anthropic, Google, Microsoft, and OpenAI, later joined by additional frontier AI developers. It is a membership organization whose stated purpose is advancing frontier AI safety research, identifying best practices and technical standards, and informing policymakers and civil society. It also helped establish an associated AI Safety Fund to support independent safety research.
justification: Its primary activity is operating as a membership association of frontier AI companies that develops shared industry practices and represents members' collective interests to policymakers.

alternates.justification: Much of its output is technical and professional practice guidance for AI safety practitioners.

alternates.naics_title: Research and Development in the Social Sciences and Humanities
alternates.justification: It commissions and publishes policy and governance research on frontier AI risk.

alternates.naics_title: Other Similar Organizations (except Business, Professional, Labor, and Political Organizations)
alternates.justification: As a nonprofit multi-stakeholder body it could fall in this residual membership category.

category_justification: It is explicitly a membership body founded and funded by named frontier AI companies to coordinate and represent their collective safety and policy positions.

name: GE Vernova
description: GE Vernova is a publicly traded U.S. energy technology company spun off from General Electric in April 2024 and headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts. It designs and manufactures equipment for electricity generation and delivery through three segments: Power (gas, steam, nuclear, and hydro turbines), Wind (onshore and offshore turbines), and Electrification (grid equipment and software). It also provides installation, servicing, and digital solutions for utilities and industrial power customers worldwide.
naics_title: Turbine and Turbine Generator Set Units Manufacturing
justification: Its largest lines of business are manufacturing gas, steam, hydro, and wind turbines and generator sets for electricity generation.

alternates.justification: Its Electrification segment produces grid switchgear and substation apparatus.

alternates.naics_title: Power, Distribution, and Specialty Transformer Manufacturing
alternates.justification: Grid Solutions also manufactures power and distribution transformers.
It delivers substantial engineering, installation, and plant-servicing work alongside equipment sales.

category_justification: GE Vernova is a for-profit corporation listed on the NYSE under ticker GEV.

name: GENIA AI
description: GENIA is a public benefit corporation registered in Jacksonville, Florida that builds and deploys artificial intelligence systems across Latin America and the wider Western Hemisphere. It develops platforms including GALAPAGOS, which applies machine learning to industrial and manufacturing operations, and CiudadanIA, aimed at public sector and citizen-facing applications, and it also runs the RaceFor.AI network. Its services span AI strategy, data science and machine learning development, regulatory compliance frameworks, and AI talent development for governments, universities, and private firms.
justification: Its primary activity is developing bespoke AI and machine learning software and platforms for client organizations across Latin America.

alternates.justification: It integrates and deploys AI systems into client industrial and public-sector environments.

alternates.naics_title: Other Scientific and Technical Consulting Services
alternates.justification: A substantial share of the work is AI strategy, regulatory compliance, and technical advisory.
GALAPAGOS and CiudadanIA are branded platform products it licenses to customers.

category_justification: Its own RFI submission identifies it as GENIA Latinoamerica, P.B.C., a for-profit public benefit corporation selling AI platforms and services.

name: Gecko Robotics
description: Gecko Robotics is a Pittsburgh-based private company that builds wall-climbing and submersible robots that collect ultrasonic and visual condition data from industrial assets such as boilers, tanks, pipelines, and naval vessels. The robotic inspection data feeds Cantilever, the company's AI-driven software platform that models asset health and informs maintenance and capital decisions for energy, manufacturing, and defense customers. The company raised $125 million in 2025 at a valuation above $1 billion and is expanding its own robot manufacturing capacity.
justification: Its primary commercial activity is performing robot-delivered nondestructive testing and structural condition inspection of client infrastructure, which is a testing service rather than equipment sales.

alternates.naics_title: All Other Miscellaneous General Purpose Machinery Manufacturing
alternates.justification: The company designs and manufactures its own climbing inspection robots, and is adding manufacturing capacity.
The Cantilever platform is a licensed AI software product and a growing share of the business.

alternates.naics_title: Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology)
alternates.justification: Substantial in-house robotics and sensing engineering development underlies the products.

category_justification: Venture-backed for-profit corporation selling inspection robots and software to industrial and defense customers.

name: Getty Images
description: Getty Images is a publicly traded visual content company that licenses still images, video, music, and editorial media through its Getty Images, iStock, and Unsplash brands. It maintains a large archive sourced from staff photographers, contributors, and partner agencies, and licenses that content to media, corporate, and advertising customers via web platforms and APIs. The company has also been an active party in litigation and policy debates over the use of copyrighted images to train generative AI models.
naics_title: Web Search Portals and All Other Information Services
justification: Its primary activity is operating stock photo and media libraries and licensing that archived content over the internet, the classic stock picture agency activity captured by this all-other information services code.

alternates.naics_title: Media Streaming Distribution Services, Social Networks, and Other Media Networks and Content Providers
alternates.justification: It distributes still and moving image content online as a content provider.
It commissions and employs photographers producing commercial and editorial imagery.
The business can be read as publishing and licensing copyrighted visual works.

category_justification: Publicly traded for-profit corporation (NYSE: GETY) commenting on its own commercial interests.

name: GitLab
description: GitLab Inc. is a publicly traded software company that develops and sells the GitLab DevSecOps platform, an integrated environment for source code management, continuous integration and delivery, security scanning, and AI-assisted development. The platform is offered both as a SaaS subscription and as self-managed software installed by customers, with an open-core free tier. The company operates on an all-remote model and sells primarily to enterprise engineering organizations.
justification: Its primary activity is developing and licensing a packaged software platform under subscription, whether hosted or self-managed, which is software publishing.

alternates.naics_title: Computing Infrastructure Providers, Data Processing, Web Hosting, and Related Services
alternates.justification: A large share of revenue comes from the hosted GitLab.com service, which is a hosting arrangement.
It provides implementation and integration support for enterprise DevOps deployments.
Professional services engagements involve customer-specific configuration and programming.

category_justification: For-profit publicly traded software vendor (NASDAQ: GTLB) commenting in its own commercial capacity.

name: Gladstone AI
description: Gladstone AI is a small Washington, DC-based for-profit firm that conducts technical and policy research on national security risks from advanced artificial intelligence. It authored the State Department-commissioned 2024 action plan on AI proliferation and weaponization risk and runs briefing series for congressional and executive branch audiences. Its work consists mainly of commissioned assessments, threat modeling, and advisory briefings for government clients rather than product sales.
naics_title: Other Scientific and Technical Consulting Services
justification: Its primary activity is providing commissioned technical risk assessments and advisory briefings on AI security to government clients, a scientific and technical consulting service.

alternates.naics_title: Research and Development in the Social Sciences and Humanities
alternates.justification: Much of its output is policy research on AI governance and national security.

alternates.naics_title: Administrative Management and General Management Consulting Services
alternates.justification: Its deliverables include strategy and management recommendations for federal agencies.

alternates.naics_title: Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology)
alternates.justification: It performs some technical analysis of AI system capabilities and failure modes.

category_justification: It is a privately held for-profit company; it works advisorily under contract for named government clients such as the State Department, and comments in its own capacity.

name: Goldilock
description: Goldilock is a UK-headquartered cybersecurity company whose Drawbridge product physically connects and disconnects networks, data, and operational technology assets from the internet using a hardware relay triggered out of band over non-IP channels. The approach is marketed as remote physical segmentation for critical national infrastructure, defense, and industrial control environments where software-only isolation is considered insufficient. The company sells the hardware together with a subscription control service and has worked with UK and NATO-linked defense innovation programs.
justification: Its core offering is a purpose-built network communications hardware device that performs physical layer disconnection, placing it with other communications equipment manufacturing.

alternates.justification: The product is delivered with an ongoing managed remote-isolation service, a computer-related service.

alternates.naics_title: Computer Terminal and Other Computer Peripheral Equipment Manufacturing
alternates.justification: The device can be read as a network peripheral appliance attached to customer computing systems.
A control and management software layer accompanies the hardware.

category_justification: Privately held for-profit cybersecurity vendor with commercial and defense customers.

name: HIVE
description: Hive is a San Francisco-based for-profit artificial intelligence company that sells cloud-based models through APIs for content moderation, logo and brand detection, and AI-generated and deepfake content detection. Its customers include large online platforms, advertisers, and government agencies, and it holds a US Department of Defense contract for deepfake detection. The company has been publicly active in AI policy debates, including endorsing federal legislation on digital replicas.
justification: Its primary activity is developing and licensing proprietary machine learning models as subscription software products delivered by API.

alternates.naics_title: Computing Infrastructure Providers, Data Processing, Web Hosting, and Related Services
alternates.justification: The models are delivered as a hosted API service that processes customer-supplied data at scale.
Outsourced content moderation review for platform customers is a business support service.
It builds customer-specific model integrations and custom classifiers.

category_justification: Every plausible referent for this name in an AI policy docket is a venture-backed for-profit company, and the most likely one, Hive AI, is a private AI vendor; the bare all-caps name leaves some residual ambiguity.

name: Hackensack Meridian Health
description: Hackensack Meridian Health is a nonprofit integrated health network and New Jersey's largest health system, operating roughly 18 hospitals including academic medical centers, children's hospitals, and rehabilitation facilities. It also runs ambulatory care sites, physician practices, home care, long-term care, and research institutes, and co-founded the Hackensack Meridian School of Medicine. The system employs tens of thousands of staff and is a major regional provider of acute and specialty care.
justification: The bulk of the system's operations and revenue come from general acute care hospitals providing diagnostic and medical treatment to inpatients.

alternates.naics_title: Offices of Physicians (except Mental Health Specialists)
alternates.justification: It employs a large medical group operating outpatient physician practices.
A significant portion of care is delivered through ambulatory and outpatient centers.

alternates.naics_title: Specialty (except Psychiatric and Substance Abuse) Hospitals
alternates.justification: The network includes rehabilitation and other specialty hospitals.

category_justification: It is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit health system delivering patient care and research, not a university, membership body, or government unit.

name: Health Level Seven International
description: Health Level Seven International is a nonprofit, ANSI-accredited standards development organization that creates interoperability standards for exchanging electronic health information, including HL7 v2, CDA, and FHIR. Its standards are developed through volunteer work groups drawn from a global membership of provider organizations, health IT vendors, payers, government agencies, and individual professionals, coordinated through affiliates in dozens of countries. It is headquartered in Ann Arbor, Michigan, and its standards are widely referenced in US federal health IT regulation.
justification: It is a dues-supported membership association whose primary activity is developing consensus technical standards on behalf of member organizations in the health information sector.

alternates.justification: Much of the standards work is carried out by individual health informatics professionals who join in their professional capacity.

alternates.naics_title: Other Similar Organizations (except Business, Professional, Labor, and Political Organizations)
alternates.justification: A standards development body can be treated as another type of member-based organization.

alternates.naics_title: Other Scientific and Technical Consulting Services
alternates.justification: It produces technical specifications, certification, and training services in health informatics.

category_justification: It is explicitly a membership-based standards development organization whose work groups and governance are composed of dues-paying member organizations and individuals.

name: Hispanic Tech and Telecommunications Partnership
description: The Hispanic Technology and Telecommunications Partnership (HTTP) is a Washington, DC-based nonpartisan coalition of national Latino membership and service organizations that advocates on internet, telecommunications, and technology policy. Its member organizations have included groups such as LULAC, ASPIRA Association, Hispanic Federation, and SER-Jobs for Progress National, and it advises Congress and federal agencies on broadband access, digital literacy, and technology workforce issues. Alongside policy advocacy it runs programs including a Digital Innovation Summit, Tech Innovadores, and technology policy fellowships.
justification: HTTP's primary activity is organized public-policy advocacy on telecommunications and technology issues on behalf of Latino communities, which is the defining activity of a social advocacy organization.

alternates.justification: It is a civic membership coalition of community-serving Latino organizations that also runs community programs.

alternates.naics_title: Research and Development in the Social Sciences and Humanities
alternates.justification: It self-describes as a national Latino 'think tank,' implying policy research output.

alternates.naics_title: Other Similar Organizations (except Business, Professional, Labor, and Political Organizations)
alternates.justification: A residual code for a membership coalition whose members are nonprofits rather than businesses or professionals.

category_justification: Its own boilerplate calls it 'a nonpartisan coalition of 19 national Latino organizations,' so it has an explicit organizational membership base representing members' collective interests.

name: Holistic AI
description: Holistic AI is a venture-backed private company, founded in 2020 with offices in London and New York, that sells an enterprise AI governance, risk, and compliance software platform. The platform inventories an organization's AI systems and monitors them for bias, robustness, privacy, and regulatory conformity against frameworks such as the EU AI Act and NYC Local Law 144. The company also performs AI audit and assurance engagements and publishes policy commentary on AI regulation.
justification: Its primary revenue activity is licensing a proprietary AI governance software platform to enterprise customers, which is software publishing.

alternates.naics_title: Other Scientific and Technical Consulting Services
alternates.justification: A substantial share of its work is bespoke AI audit, assurance, and regulatory-readiness advisory rather than licensed software.
Deployments frequently involve customer-specific integration and configuration work.
It designs and integrates AI risk-monitoring systems into client technology stacks.

category_justification: It is a for-profit, venture-funded commercial software vendor selling to enterprise customers, commenting in its own corporate capacity.

name: Hologic
description: Hologic, Inc. is a publicly traded (Nasdaq: HOLX) medical technology company headquartered in Marlborough, Massachusetts, focused primarily on women's health. It manufactures and sells digital mammography and breast-imaging X-ray systems, molecular diagnostic assays and instruments, and surgical devices, organized into Diagnostics, Breast Health, Surgical, and Skeletal Health segments. The SEC assigns it SIC 3844, X-Ray Apparatus and Tubes and Related Irradiation Apparatus.
justification: Hologic's flagship and SEC-designated primary line is manufacturing mammography and other X-ray/irradiation imaging apparatus, which this code covers.

alternates.justification: Diagnostics is Hologic's largest reportable segment by revenue and consists largely of molecular assay reagents and test kits.
Its Surgical segment manufactures gynecologic surgical instruments and consumables.
Some imaging and diagnostic instruments are electromedical rather than irradiation apparatus.

category_justification: It is a publicly traded for-profit manufacturer, listed as 'Private sector' in the RFI respondent index.

name: Houghton Mifflin Harcourt
resolved_name: Houghton Mifflin Harcourt (HMH), a portfolio company of Veritas Capital
description: Houghton Mifflin Harcourt, which operates as HMH, is a Boston-based K-12 education company that develops and sells core curriculum, supplemental content, assessments, and instructional software to US school districts. Formerly listed on Nasdaq, it was taken private by Veritas Capital in 2022 and has since positioned itself as a connected teaching-and-learning technology company built on its longstanding educational publishing catalog. Its trade publishing division was sold separately to HarperCollins in 2021.
justification: Its primary activity remains developing and publishing K-12 textbooks and curriculum content, which NAICS places under book publishing including textbooks.

alternates.justification: A growing share of revenue comes from licensed digital learning platforms and assessment software.
It provides professional learning, coaching, and implementation services to school districts.
Its teacher professional-development business is a training service line.

category_justification: It is a for-profit private-equity-owned commercial publisher, listed as 'Private sector' in the RFI respondent index.

name: Hydra Host
description: Hydra Host is a US-based private company that provides on-demand bare-metal GPU compute and manages GPU cluster deployments for AI workloads. It operates a marketplace and management layer that matches customers needing accelerated compute with capacity in independent and underutilized data centers, which it markets as building 'AI factories.' The company rents GPU servers by the hour or on reserved terms and provides provisioning, orchestration, and monitoring software for those clusters.
naics_title: Computing Infrastructure Providers, Data Processing, Web Hosting, and Related Services
justification: Its primary activity is providing GPU computing infrastructure and hosting capacity to customers on a rental basis, which is squarely this code.

alternates.justification: It manages third-party data center GPU capacity on behalf of both suppliers and customers.
It develops a provisioning and orchestration software layer over the hardware.
Part of the model is brokering third-party data center capacity rather than owning it.
